sections.title: Autoimmune conditions — the Holistic Rx (diet, detox and lifestyle)
body: Autoimmune disease is the immune system's misguided attack on the body: excess inflammation confuses its ability to tell self from nonself, autoantibodies form against normal cells, and regulatory T cells fail to keep the response in check. There are more than eighty known autoimmune diseases, and having one makes you three times more likely to develop another.

Diet and detox special considerations: avoid nightshades (tomatoes, eggplant, potatoes, peppers), legumes/lentils, eggs, caffeine, nuts, and seeds — common food sensitivities in autoimmune disease. Fix deficiencies in calcium, iron, vitamin D, zinc, B6, B12, and folate. Eat vegetables at every meal, and favor sulfur-rich foods (cabbage, onions, garlic, leeks, cauliflower, asparagus) to help reduce symptoms; use coconut oil and olive oil for healthy fats. Raw, unprocessed honey can also boost immunity.

For thyroid autoimmunity specifically, increase fatty acids, iodine (seaweed, saltwater fish, or a multivitamin), tyrosine (red meat, chicken, seaweed, seafood), selenium (red meats, liver, chicken, turkey, fish, shellfish), zinc (red meats, chicken, seafood, seaweed), iron, omega-3s, vitamin D3, B vitamins (leafy greens, broccoli, beets, red meat, liver), and vitamin A (orange fruits/veggies, liver, kale). Kale and broccoli are goitrogens, but their benefits outweigh that concern. Avoid IV detoxification in all cases of autoimmunity.

The Four Big S's: stress management is key to healing autoimmune disease as with any chronic condition, including choosing gentler exercise — jogging and heavy weightlifting can be too harsh on the joints. Flexibility, strengthening, aerobic exercise, and body-awareness practices like tai chi, yoga, and Pilates improve posture, coordination, balance, and joint/muscular mobility. An exercise physiologist can help find what works best for you.

sections.title: Autoimmune conditions — infections and low-dose naltrexone
body: If symptoms — especially fatigue and brain symptoms — persist after three months of the foundational GutRx, consider that an infection may be contributing. A functional medicine practitioner can test for the microbe associated with your specific condition; leaky gut, stress, and inflammatory food can reactivate dormant infections and trigger the immune system. Look for coinfections (parasites, Candida, bacterial overgrowth) alongside the primary infection, and expect treatment to take time, especially with more than one infecting agent.

Table 5.1 (Autoimmunity and Infections) pairs specific autoimmune diseases with implicated microbes: autoimmunity in general with E. coli, Proteus, Klebsiella; ankylosing spondylitis with Klebsiella; Graves' disease and Hashimoto's thyroiditis with herpes, EBV, MAP, H. pylori, Yersinia, and Campylobacter; Guillain-Barré syndrome with Campylobacter, cytomegalovirus, and EBV; multiple sclerosis with Chlamydia pneumoniae, EBV, and measles; rheumatoid arthritis with Citrobacter, Klebsiella, Proteus, Porphyromonas, EBV, E. coli, hepatitis C, and mycobacterium; rheumatic fever with Streptococcus pyogenes; and SLE/lupus, autism, uveitis, keratitis, autoimmune hepatitis, polymyositis, psoriasis, ITP, IgA nephropathy, glomerulonephritis, pemphigus, Sjögren's syndrome, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and myasthenia gravis with various combinations of EBV, cytomegalovirus, herpes 1/2/6, measles, coxsackievirus, and hepatitis C.

Viral infections: chronic viral infections (herpes 1, 2, 6; Epstein-Barr virus) can hide dormant and trigger inflammation. For EBV activity, check EBV EA-D IgG (active/reactivated infection), EBV VCA IgG/IgM (past or reactivated infection), and EBV EBNA-1 IgG (past infection, or active replication in B cells when combined with a positive VCA). Treat with Lauricidin (1 tsp three times daily, an acid derived from coconut oil) and humic acid (2 pills/day) to lower viral load; L-lysine 500 mg for prevention, 1–4 g/day with food during an outbreak. Herbal options: Lomatium (can cause a one-time rash), Cordyceps (750 mg, two capsules, three times daily for ninety days), or olive leaf extract (one capsule twice daily for sixty days). Add NAC (1,800 mg/day), thymic protein A, adaptogens, vitamin D, vitamin C (500–3,000 mg/day), or lysine for additional support.

Bacterial infections: implicated bacteria include Yersinia enterocolitica (specialized stool test), H. pylori (breath, stool antigen, or blood test), SIBO (breath test), Chlamydia pneumoniae, and Bartonella or Mycobacterium avium subspecies paratuberculosis (MAP). Treatment combines antibiotics, probiotics (dosed apart from the antibiotic), caprylic acid, and an enzyme blend of cellulase, hemicellulase, xylanase, and beta-glucanase to prevent yeast overgrowth. H. pylori: zinc, berberine, bismuth citrate, mastic gum, oil pulling, and cranberry juice. Yersinia: sweet wormwood, grapefruit seed extract, berberine, black walnut, uva ursi, or doxycycline. Garlic, licorice, quercetin, CoQ10, turmeric, and oil of oregano help broadly. SIBO: rifaximin (Xifaxan), adding neomycin or tinidazole if methane-predominant. Chlamydia pneumoniae: minocycline 100 mg twice daily for three weeks.

Lyme disease: if symptoms don't improve, consider Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi), which can mimic autoimmune symptoms and affect multiple organs. Ask for advanced testing (iSpot Lyme, ELISA, western blot, Lyme PCR); antibiotic treatment may follow a positive result. Supportive foods/herbs: thyme, lemon balm, zinc, licorice root, L-lysine, lomatium root, reishi mushroom, silver hydrosol, astaxanthin, and Nascent iodine.

Fungal infections: systemic Candida is common in autoimmune disease — test with blood work and stool IgG/IgM. If positive: Diflucan 100 mg twice daily for three weeks, or nystatin 500,000 units, two capsules, three times daily for thirty to ninety days.

Parasitic infections: test for toxoplasmosis (blood) and Blastocystis hominis (stool). Treat blastocystis with Alinia 1,000 mg twice daily for three days, repeated after two weeks and again two weeks later, or nystatin as above (for fungal overgrowth alongside or after Alinia). Herbal options: CandiBactin (two capsules three times daily for sixty days), a wormwood-containing antiparasitic (600 mg twice daily for seven days, repeated in two weeks — avoid with a history of liver problems), or oil of oregano (150 mg, two capsules, three times daily for sixty days) combined with Saccharomyces boulardii (5–15 billion CFU, two to four times daily for sixty days).

Low-dose naltrexone: as an opioid antagonist, naltrexone can enhance immune function — increasing endogenous adrenaline production, reducing inflammation, and increasing regulatory T-cell cytokines including IL-1 and TGF-B — helpful for those with multiple autoimmune conditions or symptoms and very high antibodies. For autoimmunity, use only low doses, 1.5–4.5 mg/day, starting at 1.5 mg at night. It should not be a first line of defense — use it only after implementing the foundational recommendations and if symptoms persist.

sections.title: Celiac disease — the Holistic Rx
body: Celiac disease is an autoimmune reaction to gluten. Typical symptoms: recurrent bloating, cramping, abdominal pain, brain fog, weight changes, insomnia and other sleep issues, fatigue, headaches, delayed puberty, pale foul-smelling stool, peripheral neuropathy, joint pain, mood changes, thinning hair, pale mouth sores, tingling of hands/feet, vomiting, unexplained weight loss, unexplained infertility or recurrent miscarriage, and dermatitis herpetiformis (skin rash). Testing: IgA and IgG anti-gliadin antibodies, IgA anti-endomysial antibodies, tissue transglutaminase antibodies, total IgA, and genetic testing (HLA DQ2, HLA DQ8).

Supplements: supplements that heal leaky gut are key — digestive enzymes with amylase (a pancreatic enzyme, to enhance digestion), probiotics, B vitamins (B2, B3, B6, B9, B12), calcium, magnesium, zinc, and other gut-healing agents like L-glutamine, N-acetyl-D-glucosamine, and gamma oryzanol. In children, start with digestive enzymes and probiotics.

Homeopathy: early constitutional treatment from an experienced homeopath — matched to the person's most distressing symptoms — can help with celiac-related constipation, increased frequency of bulky/offensive-smelling stools, allergies, gastroenteritis, and emotional issues.
Acupressure: P6, SP6, CV12.

Aromatherapy: caraway, lavender, and bitter orange help harmonize gut bacterial balance. Peppermint oil and cumin can ease digestive symptoms; ginger and turmeric protect the stomach and support digestion. Peppermint and ginger work well together for nausea.

sections.title: Graves' disease — the Holistic Rx
body: Graves' disease is an autoimmune disorder causing overproduction of thyroid hormone. Symptoms: mood changes, racing heart, muscle pain, insomnia, digestive issues, hand/finger tremors, increased perspiration or warm moist skin, thyroid gland enlargement, irregular periods, skin-texture changes (thickened skin on the lower legs or red bumps — pretibial myxedema), and eye problems (bulging/exophthalmos, pain, redness, vision loss). Tests: TSH, free T4, free T3, thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI), and TSH receptor antibody.

Supplements: B-complex (50 mg twice daily). L-carnitine (start 2,000 mg/day, work up to 4,000 mg/day as needed) can reduce heart palpitations, tremors, insomnia, and anxiety. CoQ10 (100–400 mg/day with a fat-containing meal) helps muscle weakness and pain. Plant sterols to balance the immune system. Selenium (200 mcg/day) may slow progression of eye symptoms. Magnesium (400 mg/day) helps prevent arrhythmias. Calcium citrate 1,000 mg (ages 19–50) or 1,200 mg (women 51+ and men over 71), alongside optimized vitamin D. Bugleweed (start 2 mL three times daily, increasing to 4 mL after three days and 6 mL three days later) can prevent thyroid damage and calm the thyroid, keeping antibodies from binding to it. Motherwort liquid extract (start 2 mL daily, increase to 4 mL after five days) helps palpitations, sleep issues, appetite issues, and anxiety — talk to your doctor, and don't combine with sedating medications. Lemon balm (start 300 mg, increase to 600 mg after seven days) inhibits antibodies from binding to the thyroid gland. Glucomannan (start 1.5 g twice daily, work up to 3.0 g twice daily) decreases circulating thyroid hormone levels.

Homeopathy: Iodum 30C for someone who feels very hot, is always in a hurry, obsessive, dark-haired, and dark-eyed — also indicated for weight loss despite an increased appetite, extreme heat sensitivity, and seeking coolness. Natrum mur 30C for palpitations and constipation, in someone who looks anemic, is weak, and craves salt. Lycopus 30C for a racing, pounding heart from nervous irritation, with exophthalmos. Sulphur for heat intolerance. Pulsatilla for heat intolerance with no thirst. Lachesis for hot flashes with intolerance of tight clothing. Lycopodium for weight loss (more upper body), craving warm drinks and sweets. Phosphorus for extreme weakness with excessive, offensive stool. Others that can be used: Kali iodatum, Ferrum metallicum, Lycopodium clavatum, and Spongia tosta.
Acupressure: GV17, ST9, P6, HT7, LI4, ST30.

Aromatherapy: frankincense (two drops daily on the roof of the mouth) and myrrh (applied over the thyroid area twice daily) can help, along with anti-inflammatory oils like lavender, rose, and tea tree — combined with coconut oil, these can soothe irritated skin.

sections.title: Hashimoto's thyroiditis — the Holistic Rx
body: Hashimoto's is autoimmune thyroiditis. Symptoms: fatigue, depression and mood disorders, weight gain, feeling cold easily, digestive issues, muscular pain, joint stiffness and swelling, hair loss, frequent urination and excessive thirst, and menstrual changes. Assessment: TSH, free T4, free T3, antithyroglobulin antibody, and antithyroid peroxidase antibodies (which can appear decades before TSH is affected), plus reverse T3 and ferritin; vitamin A, selenium, and zinc can also be checked. Landmarks of healing: symptom improvement or resolution, antibody count dropping first under 100 and then under 35, and regeneration of thyroid tissue.

Supplements: probiotics. Multivitamin with vitamin A (5,000–10,000 IU/day). Vitamin E (400 IU). B vitamins: riboflavin (50 mg/day), niacin (200 mg/day), B6 (50 mg/day), folate (800 mcg/day), B12 (1,000 mcg/day of methylcobalamin), biotin (5,000 mcg/day), and B1 (600 mg/day specifically for fatigue). Iodine (150–300 mcg/day). Zinc (25–50 mg/day). Magnesium (500 mg/day). Vitamin C (1,000 mg/day). Iron glycinate (25 mg/day; keep ferritin between 50 and 100 if still menstruating). Omega-3 fish oil (1,000 mg twice daily with food). Selenium (200–400 mcg) has been shown to help regulate the hormones. Others: Antabine, shown to reduce TPO antibodies by preventing the inflammatory immune system from responding; also curcumin, Thytrophin PMG, or Drenatrophin PMG. Children with hypothyroidism: iodine (50–900 mcg/day), selenium (20–200 mcg/day), tyrosine (500 mg/day), vitamin A (200,000 IU as one dose), and seaweed/kelp (2 tbsp/day).

Homeopathy: Arsenicum 30C every twelve hours for up to five days while a constitutional remedy is being found. Calcarea carbonica for constipation (hard-then-soft stool) and heavy menses. Sepia for weak patients with a pale yellow face, feeling cold, and a sensation of bearing-down; helps control excessive hair loss — these patients crave acidic foods and pickles. Lycopodium for gastric problems with excessive flatulence, craving hot foods, weakness, and irritability. Graphites for those who tire easily, are obese, become sad when listening to music, and are constipated and timid. Nux vomica for hypothyroidism with people who are easily offended, constipated, bloated after eating, crave stimulants, and crave fatty and spicy foods; these people also feel cold.
Acupressure: ST36, P6, KD3, GV7, KD7, SP6, LI10, LI11.

Aromatherapy: frankincense can help lower thyroid antibodies when used alongside other modalities. Peppermint oil can help reduce brain fog, depression, headaches, and digestive issues. Lavender and myrtle may help restore hair and calm anxiety. Others that help hypothyroidism symptoms: lemongrass, myrrh, clove, basil, marjoram, rosemary, grapefruit, and clary sage.

sections.title: Multiple sclerosis — the Holistic Rx
body: Multiple sclerosis (MS) occurs when the immune system attacks the myelin sheath covering nerve fibers, permanently damaging the nerves and disrupting nervous-system communication. Symptoms depend on the location and extent of the damage and may include fatigue, dizziness, slurred speech, prolonged double vision, involuntary eye movement (nystagmus), tremor, bowel and bladder problems, poor coordination, numbness or weakness in one or more limbs or the trunk (often one-sided), and electric-shock sensations with certain movements (Lhermitte's sign). Diagnosis: imaging and spinal tap.

Supplements: vitamin E (400 mg of mixed tocotrienols or mixed tocopherols daily). High-potency B-complex (B-100) daily, including B6, B7 (biotin), and B12. Cyanocobalamin (1,000 mcg sublingually each day). L-methylfolate (levomefolic acid, 1,000 mcg daily). CoQ10 (200 mg daily; doses up to 2,400 mg/day have been well tolerated, though above 600 mg/day some note heartburn, digestive upset, and headaches — it may also reduce the effectiveness of blood-thinning medications). Digestive enzymes with protease, bromelain, amylase, and lipase. Algae (two to eight capsules, or up to one teaspoon of powder, daily). Alpha lipoic acid (300–600 mg/day) for nerve pain; aged garlic to lower oxidative stress and improve blood flow.

Homeopathy: Agaricus for uncoordinated eye movement, muscle spasms, twitching, poor coordination, sharp shooting pains, and weak, shaky movements. Alumina for weakness, progressive paralysis, heaviness of the lower extremities, confusion, constipation, and dry skin or mucous membranes — better in open air and damp weather, worse in the morning and in a warm room. Argentum nitricum for progressive paralysis, poor coordination, loss of balance, trembling, always feeling in a rush, and multiple phobias. Arsenicum album for anxious, pessimistic, restless people with progressive paralysis and burning sensations. Causticum for slow, progressive paralysis of the limbs, numbness of hands and feet, problems with breathing, swallowing, and speech, incontinence, and restlessness at night. Cocculus for paralysis with dizziness when trying to focus on moving objects, painful contracture of the limbs and trunk, and feeling too weak to talk loudly. Conium for paralysis of the eye muscles and ascending paralysis beginning with weakness and heaviness in the thighs and lower limbs, worse in the morning. Gelsemium sempervirens for trembling and weak muscles, heavy eyelids, double vision, numbness of the face and tongue, improvement after urination, and dizziness/drowsiness. Ignatia amara for twitching and spasms especially when MS presents after grief, with emotional upset and heightened senses. Kali phos for weakness in the back and limbs worse with exercise, leaving pain, fatigue, and possible inability to move the extremity. Lachesis when jealousy or anger worsen symptoms, more left-sided, worse premenstrually or at the start of menopause. Natrum muriaticum for optic neuritis (eye pain and temporary vision loss) with body numbness, worse in the sun, coming on after grief, low mood, and awkwardness such as dropping things. Nux vomica for those who crave alcohol and stimulants, are irritable, highly driven, and intolerant of contradiction. Magnesia phos for painful spasms of twitching or jerking, improved by pressure, friction, and warmth. Phosphorus for vision problems and incontinence with numbness in the hands and feet, craving ice-cold drinks, exaggerated reflexes, fainting easily, and episodes linked to emotional upset. Plumbum for progressive paralysis, heaviness, and wasting of the muscles, especially in the legs. Tarentula for very jerky movements of the hands, feet, and tongue.

Acupressure: GV20 (headaches, poor memory, mental disorders, ringing in the ears, fatigue, and poor sleep); GV26, P6, LU9, GB34, LU1 (anxiety or depression); GV26 (reduces muscle spasms and relieves dizziness); ST36 (improves digestion); SP6, H7, B2, B23, B13, GB20, and LV3.

Aromatherapy: relaxing oils and those that support the neurological system are important — find what works best and rotate as needed. Frankincense and helichrysum support the neurological system; frankincense can be taken internally, two drops three times daily for three weeks, then one week off, repeating the cycle, while helichrysum can be applied to the neck or temples twice daily. Basil oil and cypress oil can reduce MS symptoms by improving circulation and muscle tone. Other good choices: lavender, jasmine, neroli, geranium, ylang-ylang, and rose.

sections.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) — the Holistic Rx
body: Lupus is a chronic autoimmune condition in which the body attacks its own tissues, potentially affecting the skin, brain, heart, lungs, and blood cells. Presentation varies widely and may come on suddenly or develop slowly, and may be mild or severe, temporary or permanent. Common signs and symptoms: fatigue, joint pain, dry eyes, sun sensitivity, skin lesions that worsen with sun exposure, chest pain, a butterfly-shaped rash across the bridge of the nose and cheeks, fingers and toes that turn white or blue with cold or stress (Raynaud's phenomenon), headaches, confusion, and memory loss. Diagnosis is made via history, physical exam, and laboratory testing.

Supplements: plant sterols and sterolins (20 mg three times daily on an empty stomach). Methylsulfonylmethane (MSM) (2,000–8,000 mg daily) for its natural anti-inflammatory benefits — reduce the dose if diarrhea occurs. Digestive enzymes (1–2 capsules of a full-spectrum enzyme product with each meal). Green superfood supplements chlorella and spirulina are key for alkalizing and detoxifying the body. Boswellia (1,200–1,500 mg of a standardized extract containing 60–65 percent boswellic acids, two to three times daily) for its anti-inflammatory effects. DHEA to support adrenal hormones — have DHEA-S measured in the blood and dose to bring levels above 100 mcg/dl; the usual recommended dose is 25 mg, but confirm the right dose against your own DHEA-S level. Indole-3-carbinol (DIM), broccoli extracts, and sulforaphane all help detoxify estrogens.

Homeopathy: Arsenicum album for anxious, restless individuals with a burning sensation in the joints that feels better with warmth. Belladonna when pain and swelling come on suddenly, with hot, red joints and burning pain worse with motion. Sepia for women whose lupus flares near their menstrual cycle, with constipation, depression, irritability, a tendency to feel cold, and cravings for sweet, salty, and sour foods. Pulsatilla when symptoms improve with cold and pain wanders from joint to joint. Rhus toxicodendron for pain that increases with rest and is worse in cold and damp, with joint stiffness that improves with movement and warmth. Sulphur for strong cravings for spicy foods and ice-cold drinks, getting overheated easily, and burning pain relieved by cold applications.
Acupressure: S13 (stiff neck, headaches, ringing in the ears, weakness of the arms, and back muscle spasm/ache); GV26, SP10, SP4, SP6, SP21, LI4, LI11, LV3, LV5.

Aromatherapy: use essential oils that promote relaxation, help digestion, and support the neurological system — good starting choices are lemon verbena, lavender, rose, jasmine, and geranium. Black pepper and ginger encourage blood flow and help revive tired joints and muscles; for digestive issues, ginger oil can be taken internally, three drops, two to three times daily. Frankincense essential oil is effective at reducing inflammation and immune reactions, and helichrysum oil supports the nervous system. For skin inflammation, lavender and geranium oils work well; lemon balm or juniper in a hot bath can help detoxify the body and lower inflammation.

sections.title: Rheumatoid arthritis — the Holistic Rx
body: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) occurs when inflammation attacks the lining of the joints, in addition to a wide variety of other body systems including the eyes, lungs, heart, blood vessels, and skin. Signs and symptoms: fatigue, fever, weight loss, joint stiffness (usually worse in the morning and after inactivity), and tender, warm, swollen joints — early on it can affect the smaller joints and then progress to larger joints like wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees, and hips. Diagnosis is made via history, a physical exam, and lab work.

Supplements: gamma linolenic acid (GLA) (450–500 mg/day). Curcumin and boswellia reduce pain and inflammation in the joints — can be used alone or in a combination product. Turmeric (1,000 mg once a day). Fish oil (1–3 g of EPA/DHA per day). Others: bromelain, MSM, glucosamine, vitamin C (500–1,000 mg/day), selenium (200–400 mcg/day), vitamin E (200–400 IU/day), ginger (100–200 mg three times daily), and one of grapeseed extract (100–300 mg/day), pine bark extract (100–300 mg/day), or another antioxidant. Juvenile RA: 5-MTHF (200–400 mcg/day), vitamin C (500–1,000 mg/day), calcium (1,000 mg/day), vitamin D (1,000–4,000 IU/day), CoQ10 (10–250 mg/day), vitamin E (200–400 IU/day), fish oil (2–4 g of EPA/day), zinc (10–20 mg/day), selenium (20–200 mcg/day), and castor oil applied topically to the joints daily.

Homeopathy: Bryonia for severe pain made worse by movement, the slightest touch, or heat, and relieved by cold applications. Pulsatilla for pain that passes from one part of the body to another and is made worse by warm environments; suitable if fatty food is hard to digest and there's a tendency to feel sad. Causticum for pain accompanied by muscle spasms that tends to improve in wet weather or with warmth. Rhus tox for stiffness that tends to wear off with movement (causing restlessness), worse in cold and damp weather, after rest, or in the morning. Colchicum for stiffness and pain worse in winter and during the nighttime hours. Dulcamara for stiffness and pain worse when overheated, and in cold or damp weather. Mercurius for aches and pains worsened by heat and cold, worse at night, accompanied by offensive sweat. Ruta for pain that especially affects the tendonous insertions of muscles and large joints. Rhododendron for aches and pains worse in cold weather and during electrical storms, located in the muscles and ligaments. Calcarea hypophos for sharp pains in the wrists and hands. Aconite for sudden onset of sharp pain, worse in cold and dry weather, with general restlessness and anxiety.
Acupressure: the Yang Lin Qian point (for inflammation and joint pain); LI4, LV2, LV5, GB41, GB34.
Aromatherapy: ginger essential oil has anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects; other helpful oils include juniper, vetiver, ylang-ylang, turmeric, frankincense, myrrh, and orange essential oils.

sections.title: Cardiology — the Holistic Rx (diet, detox and lifestyle)
body: Almost all cardiac risk factors are related to lifestyle, environment, and inflammation, so treating insulin resistance and lowering inflammation are the cornerstones of preventing and healing heart disease. Add herbs and spices — turmeric, garlic, ginger, cinnamon, curry powder, rosemary, thyme, basil, chili peppers, and coriander — and focus on fiber and healthy fats. Green, black, and oolong tea are great for the heart, as they contain flavonoids and have an anticlotting effect. Increase fiber up to 50 g per day with nuts, seeds, berries, and vegetables. High-potassium foods (avocados, melons, spinach, broccoli, squash) and apple cider vinegar (helps keep the body alkaline) have been shown to improve blood pressure; omega-3 foods like grass-fed beef, wild-caught salmon, chia, and flax are great for the heart. Other foods to focus on: pomegranate juice (8 oz)/seeds, watercress, goji berries, apples, capers, olives, onions, green pepper, and scallions. Limit/eliminate alcohol and caffeine, and eat about an ounce of dark chocolate daily. Detoxify the environment from lead, cadmium, and mercury.

The Four Big S's: stress raises blood pressure — it constricts blood vessels and worsens heart disease — so a daily relaxation technique is important. Moderate exercise lowers insulin resistance, inflammation, and blood pressure (consult a doctor before starting a program, as some conditions need to be addressed first). Chiropractic care can also improve cardiovascular problems.

sections.title: Atherosclerosis / coronary heart disease — the Holistic Rx
body: Coronary heart disease is a chronic disease in which plaque (a waxy substance) builds up over many years inside the coronary arteries that supply oxygen-rich blood to the heart. Symptoms: chest pain or pain radiating into the arm, neck, jaw, or back (may feel like indigestion), shortness of breath, sleep issues, and fatigue; pain can be triggered by stress and worsens with activity — any chest pain warrants an immediate ER visit. Once an acute event has passed, preventing another is accomplished with lifestyle changes.

Labs: micronutrient testing, carotid doppler, stress testing, coronary artery calcium scoring, and carotid intima-media thickness testing (especially once past age fifty, or if smoking, high cholesterol, or a family history of vascular disease) — plus Endo-PAT testing for those with known or suspected disease. Advanced lipid testing breaks lipoprotein particles down by size/subclass (small, dense, oxidized particles are the ones that squeeze through vessel-wall cracks and seed plaque) and also flags oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and inflammation markers. A comprehensive nutrition panel (e.g., ION panel) evaluates amino acids, vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, fats, urinary organic acids (how effectively the body turns food into energy), and heavy metals — correcting deficiencies found here, alongside lifestyle change, can meaningfully lower cardiovascular risk. A lipoprotein(a) test helps detect early cardiovascular disease, especially alongside an abnormal calcium score or thickened carotid artery — always look at the whole picture rather than any single value.

Supplements: fish oil (1 tablespoon daily). B vitamins — B1, B3/niacin (500 mg two to three times daily), B6 (50 mg/day), B9, B12. Taurine (3 g twice daily). CoQ10 (100–300 mg daily) — an antioxidant that protects the heart and vessels from free-radical damage and helps stabilize blood sugar. Garlic/Allium sativum (1,200 mg/day) — antioxidant and natural blood-thinning properties; reduces cholesterol and homocysteine. Curcumin (500–1,000 mg/day). Magnesium (500 mg daily) for circulation and blood pressure. Carotenoids. Others: quercetin (250–1,000 mg/day), choline (do not exceed 3,500 mg/day; pair with B vitamins, particularly pantothenic acid), grapeseed extract (300 mg/day), L-citrulline (500 mg/day), sytrinol (150 mg/day), ALA (300 mg twice daily), PQQ (20 mg/day), pterostilbene (50 mg/day), ribose (5 g two to three times daily — mitochondrial energy production), NAC (600 mg/day), resveratrol (250 mg/day), alpha-lipoic acid, L-theanine, green tea extract, ashwagandha, berberine (500–1,000 mg/day), selenium, red yeast rice (1,200–2,400 mg daily — lowers LDL and reduces heart-related deaths), and hawthorn (500–900 mg daily — improves circulation to the heart and lowers blood pressure). Cactus for angina, especially with the sensation of a band tightening around the chest.

sections.title: Hyperlipidemia — the Holistic Rx
body: One in three Americans has elevated cholesterol. Statins block HMG-CoA reductase, the liver enzyme that drives cholesterol production, thereby lowering blood cholesterol — but among people who take a statin for five years, only about one in eighty-three lives is saved, one in one hundred develops diabetes, one in ten suffers muscular damage, and roughly 18 percent develop undesirable side effects (liver dysfunction, memory loss, increased cancer risk, anemia, sexual dysfunction). Statins also block CoQ10, an antioxidant enzyme central to cellular energy production, heart function, and blood-glucose regulation. Some people do benefit from a statin — always discuss risks versus benefits with your doctor, as alternatives exist depending on your situation.

Supplements: fish oil (1–2 g EPA/DHA per day) to reduce cholesterol and triglycerides. CoQ10 (200–300 mg daily), especially if on lipid-lowering medication. Red yeast rice (start 600 mg twice daily, up to 1,200 mg twice daily at bedtime; take 25–100 mg CoQ10 alongside to prevent deficiency; look for a citrinin-free product). Niacin (1,500–3,000 mg/day if diabetic — high doses can raise blood sugar). B5/pantothenic acid. Chromium. Choline. Phytosterols/plant sterols and stanols (2,000 mg/day). Others: garlic (500 mg/day) lowers cholesterol and raises HDL; berberine (500 mg two to three times daily); guggul (1,500 mg/day standardized to 5% guggulsterones, equivalent to 75 mg guggulsterones — raises HDL, lowers cholesterol); glucomannan (two to four capsules fifteen minutes before meals with a glass of water); artichoke extract (500 mg three times daily); acetyl-L-carnitine (1,000 mg daily) for high triglycerides.
Children: fish oil (EPA/DHA 1–2 g daily), pycnogenol (50–100 mg daily), vitamin B3 (5–20 mg daily), decaf green tea (4–6 cups daily), psyllium (6 g daily), plant sterols (2–2.5 g daily).

Homeopathy: Allium sativum for excessive meat-eaters with belching, burning, and increased appetite. Aurum metallicum for a rapid pulse, depression, or anger, with pain behind the sternum especially at night. Baryta muriaticum for elderly patients with vertigo and heaviness. Nux vomica for those who crave alcohol and fatty foods. Calcarea carbonica for those who are overweight, cold-sensitive, with continuous scalp perspiration and tight, palpitating chest. Lycopodium for a desire for sweets with flatulence and other digestive symptoms.
Acupressure: Liver point, LI11, LI4, and LV3.

Aromatherapy: essential oils can lower cholesterol by decreasing emotional stress and improving circulation, with cardio-supportive and antioxidant properties — lavender, cypress, and rosemary oil support overall heart health.

sections.title: Hypertension — the Holistic Rx
body: Hypertension (high blood pressure) reflects resistance to blood flow in the arteries and the volume of blood the heart pumps. Most people are asymptomatic, though some have headaches, nosebleeds, or shortness of breath with severe hypertension. Diagnosis is made by history and office blood-pressure measurement.

Supplements: if already on BP medication, talk to your doctor first — these can lower pressure further and combining can be dangerous. Omega-3 fatty acids (1,000–2,000 mg daily EPA/DHA) reduce blood pressure with long-term use. Magnesium (500 mg daily) relaxes smooth muscle. CoQ10 (100–300 mg daily) reduces blood pressure and supports heart health — if on warfarin, monitor levels, as it can lower them (GI side effects can occur). Garlic (600 mg aged extract). Others: vitamin C (600 mg daily) induces sodium diuresis; L-arginine (4–8 g/day) or L-citrulline (2–4 g/day); hawthorn/Crataegus oxyacantha (250 mg standardized extract three times daily) dilates artery walls and lowers blood pressure; hibiscus tea (1.25 g steeped in 240 mL water, three times daily). If on diuretics: calcium (750 mg), potassium (100 mg), vitamin B1 (300 mg), P5P/B6 (50 mg), zinc (25 mg), magnesium glycinate (240 mg/day). If on a beta blocker: CoQ10 (start 200–300 mg/day) and melatonin (6 mg at bedtime).
Children: fish oil (EPA/DHA 1–2 g daily), magnesium (200–400 mg daily), arginine (1–2 g daily).

Homeopathy (hypertension and atherosclerosis): Arsenicum album for those who are pale, thin, and cold-sensitive with alternating weakness and vascular lesions; also (15C) for lipid disorders. Arsenicum iodatum to help prevent arterial sclerosis, preventive or curative (five pellets daily to once weekly). Baryta carbonica for elderly patients with high blood pressure, memory disorders, headaches, fatigue, palpitations, and possible aneurysm. Sulphur for hyperphagic, congestive presentations. Thuja occidentalis for truncal obesity. Natrum sulphuricum 15C for heaviness of trunk/shoulders/hips with a tendency to joint pain, bronchitis, and frequent diarrhea. Natrum muriaticum for high blood pressure after emotional upset, salt cravings, intense thirst, sun intolerance, desire to be alone, headaches, palpitations, and insomnia. Phosphorus for labile hypertension with salt cravings, nervousness, and frequent fainting spells. Vanadium for frequent fainting, dizziness, a sense of chest compression, confusion, and mental deterioration. Glonoinum for a pounding arterial sensation with tachycardia, congestion, a tight headache, flushed face, and throbbing carotid pain worse with heat, sun, or alcohol. Arnica to limit hemorrhage/edema and prevent thrombosis via its action on capillaries. Arsenicum metallicum (9C daily) for anxious, depressive patients with hypertensive vascular erethism, palpitations, extrasystoles, and hot flashes that improve with hot air. Aconitum for acute hypertensive attacks with a congested face, tense pulse, severe headache, palpitations, anxiety, and agitation. Argentum nitricum for stress-triggered symptoms with cravings for salt and sweets. Belladonna for a flushed face, pounding headaches, and immediate heat with cold hands/feet and light sensitivity. Lachesis for suspicious, jealous, talkative patients who feel warm and congested, are intolerant of anything touching the neck, bruise easily, and are prone to hypertension around menopause that improves with bleeding (menses, nosebleed). Nux vomica for stress-driven hypertension with irritability, impatience, stimulant/alcohol cravings, overeating, digestive issues, chilliness, and constipation, improving after a short nap. Ignatia for sudden BP spikes with hypersensitivity to worry and frustration. Calcarea fluorica for early-onset atherosclerosis with ligament hyperlaxity. Lycopodium for heart disease with cholesterol, liver, uric-acid, or kidney issues. Plumbum metallicum for renal insufficiency and thin arteries, especially in the elderly. Silicea for thin patients prone to osteoporosis and chronic suppurations. Calcarea carbonica (15C) for familial obesity with a tendency to diabetes, polyps, and kidney/gallbladder stones.
Acupressure: ST36, H7, LI11, P6, LV2 (acute stage), LV3 (during remission); GB20, K3, B38, CV17 (chest tension with stress); GV20, LI4, K1, GB34.

Aromatherapy: essential oils decrease emotional and oxidative stress while dilating arteries — lavender, ylang-ylang, frankincense, geranium, mandarin, marjoram, eucalyptus citriodora, yarrow, and clary sage calm the body and lower blood pressure. A juniper oil massage helps break down fatty deposits in the body and arteries. For atherosclerosis specifically: lemon, ginger, black pepper, basil, linalool, rosemary, cineole, and juniper.

sections.title: Dental health — the Holistic Rx (diet, detox and lifestyle)
body: Healing the gut, keeping blood sugar regulated, and creating an alkaline environment is key in healing tooth decay and getting you on the path to remineralization. Four things can contribute to tooth decay: lack of minerals in the diet, like magnesium, calcium, and phosphorus; lack of fat-soluble vitamins like D, A, E, and K; too much sugar consumption; and too much phytic-acid-rich foods. Limit foods high in phytic acid — grains, nuts, seeds, and legumes — especially when starting out the process of remineralization, and incorporate soups with gut-healing bone broth daily.

Eat high amounts of fat-soluble vitamins and healthy fats from fermented cod liver oil, grass-fed organic raw dairy (if tolerated, eat butter), seafood, and coconut oil. Focus on bone broths and organ and gland meats like bone marrow and liver to help boost the endocrine system and balance hormones. Monitor sweet intake, including maple syrup, fruit, and honey. Activator X — important for tooth mineralization and bright, healthy teeth — is found primarily in grass-fed butter and raw milk; aim for 1–1½ tablespoons per day of grass-fed butter if tolerated. Other foods to incorporate for healthy teeth: zucchini, string beans, kale, chard, seaweed, vegetable juice, and fermented foods. Cranberry juice has anti-adhesion properties and can decrease bad bacteria in the mouth.

Add a remineralizing or special probiotic toothpaste and practice oil pulling to support tooth and gum health. To help prevent gum disease, aim the toothbrush at the gum line while brushing. Charcoal can help whiten teeth. To further optimize oral health, use colloidal silver (swish and swallow, one teaspoon, three times per day for sixty seconds) and spray xylitol on the gums three times per day.

The Four Big S's: lowering stress and getting enough sleep have a large impact on oral health — they help stabilize hormones and optimize calcium and other nutrient levels in the body. Practicing gratitude daily will keep you smiling.

sections.title: Acne — the Holistic Rx
body: Pores are open to allow hair growth and to secrete sebum (oil) from the sebaceous glands. When pores get blocked, excess oil builds up and triggers rapid growth of Propionibacterium acnes — the more bacteria present, the more breakouts occur — and the resulting inflammation forms a pimple. Pores can be blocked by dead skin cells, overactive oil glands, P. acnes, and inflammation, leading to whiteheads, blackheads, and cysts. Elevated blood sugar increases acute inflammation and the inflammatory response behind breakouts, so regulating blood sugar and healing the gut are important steps in managing acne. Diagnosis is made via history and exam.

Supplements: Zinc (50 mg twice daily with meals for three months, then can reduce to 50 mg daily); can take copper (3–5 mg) along with the zinc, since zinc sulfate isn't easily absorbed. Nicotinamide combo (750 mg nicotinamide, zinc 25 mg, copper 1.5 mg, folic acid 500 mcg per day, plus daily vitamin B6) for four to eight weeks can reduce pimples. Tea tree oil (5% solution diluted in water, dabbed onto blemishes twice daily) can act similarly to benzoyl peroxide. Vitex (chasteberry) (160 mg of a standardized Vitex extract) reduces acne formation. Others: vitamin A (2,000–4,000 IU daily) reduces oil and keratin production — going over the upper limit can be a problem, and it can be dangerous for pregnant women; prenatal vitamins should not contain more than 3,000 IU of preformed vitamin A. Burdock root (Arctium lappa) (300–500 mg capsule, or thirty drops of tincture, or 1 cup of tea, three times daily). Topical steam treatment: pour boiling water over strawberry leaves, eucalyptus, thyme, and wintergreen; place a towel over the head and lean over the bowl for ten to fifteen minutes. Natural clay mask: bentonite clay or Fuller's earth mixed with rose water into a paste, left on for 10 minutes. Children: vitamin A (1,000–5,000 IU daily), B3 (4% niacinamide wash applied topically daily), zinc (10 mg daily).

Homeopathy: Antimonium crudum helps acne associated with digestive disorders. Calcarea sulphurica can help chronic or cystic acne presenting with a yellowish discharge. Hepar sulphuris calcareum helps acne filled with pus that is painful to touch and improves with warmth. Ledum palustre helps pustular acne on the nose and cheeks that feels better with cold. Pulsatilla is for acne associated with hormonal changes. Silicea is for chronic white pustules. Selenium is best for acne accompanied by hyperseborrhea and hair loss. Sulphur is for inflamed, sore, red acne worsened by heat, in a patient who is also impatient, irritable, and moody — washing or heat can aggravate symptoms. Nux vomica is indicated for acne aggravated by excessive medications, stimulants, or rich food. Kali bromatum is for teenagers who are easily depressed and anxious, with acne and anxiety shown through nonstop movement. Eugenia jambosa is for acne with a small white suppuration spot at its center.
Acupressure: LI4, LU5, CV9. Others: GB14, SP10, B23, B47, ST2, B10.

Aromatherapy: Lavender oil, geranium, and bergamot (an astringent and antidepressant) can help improve inflammation. Once the skin improves, apply a lotion made with diluted water, lavender, and orange blossom to reduce scarring. Others that can help: clove, geranium, lavender, and tea tree oils. Clary sage, juniper, lemongrass, mandarin, and lemon can help with blackheads.

sections.title: Eczema — the Holistic Rx
body: Eczema is a chronic skin condition where an itchy, red rash appears over the body. Symptoms include dry, red, inflamed, sensitive skin, intense itching, recurring rash, scaly areas, and rough, leathery patches that can be accompanied by oozing or crusting. Diagnosis is made via history and physical exam.

Supplements: Essential fatty acids (1–2 g EPA/DHA daily, or 2 tbsp of flaxseed oil daily). Evening primrose oil (3 g daily) or borage oil contains GLA and can be used orally or topically. Vitamin E (400 IU) helps the body use fatty acids and promotes wound healing. Burdock root (300 mg capsule or 1 mL of tincture) helps cleanse the skin; vitamin C with bioflavonoids (1–3 g daily) improves the immune system; natural creams with chamomile; licorice root gel 2% (to reduce inflammation and itching); zinc (50 mg three times daily for six weeks); copper (2 mg daily); black cumin seed oil (20–40 mg daily per pound of body weight), taken orally or mixed into lotion for the skin; neem oil; quercetin (500–1,000 mg three to four times daily) as an anti-inflammatory; and turmeric, which is also anti-inflammatory. Improve wound healing with B5, vitamin C, zinc, and fatty acids. Children: fish oil (EPA/DHA 1,000–4,000 mg daily), probiotics, vitamin D (1,000–4,000 IU per day), zinc (10–20 mg daily).

Homeopathy by phase: erythematous phase — apis, urticaria urens, belladonna. Vesicular phase — rhus toxicodendron, rhus vernix or rhus venenata, mezereum, cantharis, anagallis arvensis, croton tiglium. Exudative phase — graphites, mezereum, petroleum, antimonium crudum, viola tricolor. Desquamative phase — arsenicum album, arsenicum iodatum, natrum sulphuricum, berberis vulgaris, hydrocotyle asiatica. Fissure phase — nitricum acidum, graphites, antimonium crudum, petroleum, sepia.

Homeopathy for itching and individual presentations: staphysagria (itching on eyelids and genitals), cistus canadensis (red, oozing, scabby lesions on cheeks and backs of hands), manganum aceticum (itching of joint creases with scales or fissures), radium bromatum (burning, itching thick skin), dolichos pruriens (itching with constipation), chamomilla (itching that causes behavioral disturbance). Arsenicum album is for tender, dry, itchy, swollen skin eruptions, worse in winter, with itching intense between midnight and 2:00 a.m.; the patient feels restless. Alumina is for dry, itchy skin in a constipated person. Calendula soothes affected inflamed areas topically. Calcarea carbonica helps eczema that's worse in winter, with clammy hands and feet and cravings for sweets and eggs — a great remedy for cradle cap. Graphites is for eczema mainly affecting the palms and areas behind the ears, with dry, thick, honey-like discharge, and itching intensified by a warm bed. Hepar sulph is for skin that is easily infected and sensitive, worse in the cold. Medorrhinum helps those who've had eczema since very young — they tend to be warm, sweat easily, and crave ice and oranges. Mezereum is for blistering eczema that oozes and crusts, feeling better in open air and cold. Petroleum is for dry, cracked skin on the palms and hands, itching worse at night and with warmth of the bed. Psorinum is for eczema that looks dirty, is irritated, and is prone to infection, scratched until it bleeds, with general chilliness. Rhus toxicodendron is for itchy, blistering eczema that improves with warmth and movement, craving cold milk, itching worse at night or in damp weather. Sulphur helps when skin is red, rough, itchy, and dry, with early-morning diarrhea, aggravated by heat and washing.
Acupressure: LI11 (helps with itching), B40, SP10, B23, B47, ST36, B10, LI4, LU9, B13. Weeping eczema: SP9, B52, CV9. Severe itching: LU7, SP10, LV5, B13.

Aromatherapy: essential oils can help soothe inflammation and itching, including juniper, peppermint, bergamot, carrot, jojoba, lavender, frankincense, thyme, benzoin, sweet marjoram, geranium, and chamomile.
Other Recommendations: biofeedback and climatotherapy (using water and sunlight as therapy) can also be helpful.

sections.title: Alopecia (Hair Loss) — the Holistic Rx
body: Hair loss, or alopecia, can occur at any age and in any gender and can be due to multiple causes, including medication side effects, hormonal issues, and nutritional deficiencies (e.g., ferritin). Diagnosis can be made with a detailed history, examination, and testing, including biopsy.

Supplements: Saw palmetto (320 mg daily) improves hair growth. Pygeum (100 mg twice daily) slows hair loss and improves prostate health. Pumpkin seed oil (8 g, or 1 tbsp, daily). Aloe vera juice (1/2 cup twice daily). B vitamins like biotin (2,000–3,000 mcg daily) and pantothenic acid (100 mg per day). Others: silicon (orthosilicic acid); MSM (1,000–3,000 mg daily), which promotes hair development; bamboo extract (900 mg twice daily). Aurum muriaticum helps hair loss associated with headaches and boils on the head, symptoms worse at night, with a high likelihood of depression. Fluoric acidum helps brittle hair that falls out in little tufts. Selenium helps painful, sensitive skin with loss of body hair as well. Arnica is for hair loss associated with severe injury. Kali carbonicum helps hair loss associated with dryness of hair and scalp. Baryta carb helps hair loss in an elderly, mentally slow person with poor circulation. Ignatia amara is for hair loss that comes on with acute grief or emotional trauma. Lycopodium clavatum is for hair loss after childbirth and for premature balding and graying. Natrum muriaticum is for hair loss with dandruff and white crusts on the scalp, with depression and salt cravings. Phosphoric acidum is for hair loss after extreme emotion and grief, with a fatigued, indifferent patient. Sepia is for hair loss associated with hormonal changes, like after childbirth or at menopause. Silica (Silicea) is helpful when hair loss accompanies a chronic illness — the hair is brittle and the person tends to be thin, chilly, and easily fatigued. Phosphorus helps with hair that falls out in handfuls.
Acupressure: Baihui point (improves blood circulation), hollow point, ST36.
Aromatherapy: rosemary, lavender, clary sage, and cypress can stimulate hair growth; jasmine, rose, and geranium have relaxing properties. These can be added to homemade shampoos.

sections.title: Psoriasis — the Holistic Rx
body: Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition of the skin characterized by thick plaques. Diagnosis is via history, examination, and possible biopsy.

Supplements: Digestive enzymes (one to two capsules with each meal) help digest effectively. Hydrochloric acid (one to three capsules with each meal, decreasing the dose if a burning sensation occurs) helps with protein digestion. Optimize vitamin D and B12. Others: milk thistle (70–210 mg three times per day), sarsaparilla (250–500 mg three times per day) to reduce bacterial toxin effects; a good multivitamin with 25,000 IU of vitamin A (a critical nutrient for healthy skin), 400 IU of vitamin E, 800 mcg folic acid, 200 mcg selenium, 200 mcg chromium, 25–50 mg zinc, and other antioxidants; burdock root, cleavers, barberry, calendula, and oil of anise. Topical aloe vera (0.5%) cream has been effective for psoriasis. Creams that help contain avocado oil, B12, and Oregon grape (10%) cream. Others to try: creams with vitamin E, vitamin A, zinc, sarsaparilla, and goldenseal. Psoriatic arthritis: evening primrose, borage, fish oil, curcumin, bromelain, and quercetin. Children: fish oil (1–2 g EPA/DHA per day), vitamin A (1,000–4,000 IU daily), vitamin D (0.005% applied topically three times a day), aloe vera gel (three times daily), Oregon grape root (10% cream applied three times daily).

Homeopathy: Arsenicum iodatum helps dry, scaly, itchy skin that leaves large scales when exfoliated, leaving a raw, exuding surface, with a weak, exhausted patient who sweats profusely. Kali sulphuricum is indicated for scaly dermatosis. Arsenicum album helps restless, anxious patients with dry, itchy, scaly plaques that feel like burning skin, improving with warm applications. Belladonna can treat rectal psoriasis. Calcarea carbonica is for dry, scaly plaques that often open up, in a person who is fatigued, overwhelmed, anxious, overweight, and chilly, craving eggs, dairy, and sweets. Graphites may help psoriasis affecting the skin behind the ears, backs of the hands, scalp/head, and genitals, with honey-colored oozing pus, worse at night. Kali arsenicosum helps extremely scaly lesions aggravated by warmth. Petroleum is for a condition aggravated by cold, worse in winter, with dry, itchy skin worsened by the warmth of the bed. Mercurius solubilis helps those with swollen lymph nodes and greasy-looking skin that becomes easily infected, in introverted people with strong emotions who are sensitive to temperature changes. Mezereum is for fine, white, scaly psoriasis covering large areas, with crusting and itching that feels better with cold. Rhus toxicodendron helps psoriasis that is raw, itchy, red, dry, and chapped, improving with heat or baths, in a person who craves milk and is restless. Sepia is one of the most common remedies for psoriasis, with thickening of the skin, circular eruptions, and dryness, often on the elbow — recommended for women with hormonal imbalance who feel chilly and irritable. Staphysagria helps when psoriasis affects the scalp and erupts after suppressed grief or emotions. Sulphur helps dry, scaly, red, itchy/burning patches that are often moist and oozing, worse after baths and from warmth — used for psoriatic arthritis and when the person often feels too hot.
Acupressure: GB20, LI4, LV3, ST36, and B10.

Aromatherapy: essential oils can bring relief to inflamed skin and support healing, including lavender oil (especially for stress and inflammation), frankincense, tea tree, myrrh, geranium, and carrot seed oil (scalp psoriasis). Coconut oil can be used as the base oil — always check a small test patch first to make sure you aren't reacting to a specific oil. Juniper baths may also be helpful.

sections.title: Rosacea — the Holistic Rx
body: Rosacea is a chronic inflammatory condition of the skin on the cheeks, chin, eyelids, nose, or forehead that becomes inflamed and red. There are often small red bumps or pustules on the affected areas, small spider-like blood vessels on the face, a red nose, and a tendency to blush or flush easily; over time it can give the nose a swollen, waxy look. Common triggers are emotional stress, hot or cold weather, sunshine, spicy food, MSG, vinegar, cinnamon oil, alcohol, and occasionally some skincare products — even links to Candida have been noted. High doses of B6 and B12 can trigger rosacea. Diagnosis can be made via history and exam.

Supplements: betaine hydrochloride (one to three capsules with each meal, reducing the dose if burning occurs) improves digestion. Licorice helps reduce inflammation and soothe irritation. Feverfew helps reduce redness and dryness — choose a parthenolide-free extract. Nicotinamide combo (750 mg, zinc 25 mg, copper 1.5 mg, folic acid 500 mcg) helps improve symptoms after four to eight weeks. Zinc (60–70 mg per day for no more than three months, then 15–20 mg per day). Others: azelaic acid topical cream (3–10%), gentian root (300 mg, or ten to twenty drops, five to fifteen minutes before meals to improve digestion), burdock root (300 mg or 3 mL three times per day) improves detoxification and hormone balance; natural progesterone has anti-inflammatory benefits and improves skin conditions; B vitamin (50 mg twice daily), especially B12 (400–800 mcg sublingually daily); pancreatin (350–500 mg before meals); and brewer's or nutritional yeast (1½ tsp daily). Turmeric, ginger, aloe vera gel, and raw honey applied to the skin have also been shown to improve symptoms.

Homeopathy: Arsenicum album helps anxious people who get cold easily, with lesions that are hot, dry, and flaky, and who prefer warm drinks. Pulsatilla is for rosacea that feels better in fresh air and worse in warm rooms, with symptoms associated with hormonal changes like puberty or menopause, in individuals who are weepy, sensitive, and crave sweets. Sepia is for rosacea associated with hormonal changes in a woman who is fatigued and irritable, craves salty, sour, and sweet foods, and has a tendency toward depression. Sulphur helps chronic redness and inflammation aggravated by heat, sun, and warmer climates, in a person who prefers coolness. Carbo animalis is for facial lesions of rosacea. Arnica montana is a remedy for papulo-pustules. Sanguinaria canadensis helps rosacea with burning sensations and itching, hot flushes with redness of the cheeks, aggravated by heat. Eugenia jambosa is indicated for rosacea common in alcoholics, who often have cramps in the feet. Calcarea fluorica helps those with severe telangiectasias. Lachesis mutus is prescribed for rhinophyma, especially when symptoms are aggravated by hormonal changes. Thuja occidentalis helps those with rosacea accompanied by varicose veins on the cheeks.
Acupressure: the Yin Tang point, LI20, SI18, ST4, LI4, ST36, SP10, ST3, B10 (helps with anxiety and stress).
Aromatherapy: tea tree oil, eucalyptus, geranium, chamomile, rose, rosemary, thyme, and lavender essential oil can help relieve skin inflammation — try applying with a cool compress.

sections.title: Ear, Nose, and Throat — the Holistic Rx (diet, detox and lifestyle)
body: Lowering overall inflammation allows the body to heal and improves ear, nose, and throat symptoms. Garlic and onions boost immune function (high in vitamin C, speed recovery, improve circulation); other anti-inflammatory foods include flax, chia, and cold-pressed oils. Apple cider vinegar (1 tsp mixed with water and a little lemon juice) can lower inflammation at the first sign of an allergy attack. Nutritional deficiencies can cause dizziness, so optimize green leafy vegetables for B vitamins; caffeine and alcohol worsen immune function and dizziness.

If you have a tree pollen allergy, consider limiting apples, peaches, pears, kiwi, plums, and nectarines, plus carrots, fennel, green peppers, and celery, along with almonds, walnuts, hazelnuts, and spices like basil, paprika, and coriander. If you have a grass and weed pollen allergy, avoid melons, bananas, cucumbers, echinacea, chamomile, parsley, paprika, dill, oregano, tarragon, and pepper.

Detoxing your environment helps you avoid allergens: a room humidifier with warm mist during dry conditions is beneficial (especially with a forced-hot-air furnace); clean air ducts every two to three years, and change the furnace filter monthly during winter; use negative ions or an air cleaner, especially with moldy air and air-conditioning; clean carpets regularly with a HEPA or water-filter vacuum cleaner and environmentally friendly cleaning agents. Avoid the outdoors when pollen and pollution are high (cold temperatures minimize pollen); check the local pollen count (pollen.com); pollen is higher on sunny, dry, windy days and mornings, lower on windless, cool, moist days. Wear sunglasses, keep windows and doors closed, wash bed linens in hot water weekly, follow a no-shoes-indoors policy, keep dirty clothes in a covered hamper, and trim pet fur. Avoid fans that draw in outside air; use air-conditioning. For year-round allergies, use blinds instead of curtains, dust-mite covers on pillows, and washable area rugs instead of wall-to-wall carpet on hardwood floors. Follow the water/air/living-environment/kitchen/body detox recommendations from chapter 2.

Flushing pollen from the nasal passages eases sinus pressure, congestion, and inflammation: use a neti pot in the morning and before bed with 8 oz of warm water (never tap water) mixed with 1/4 tsp of salt, or premixed saline.

The Four Big S's — special consideration: stress worsens inflammation, so managing stress is key to healing. Release negative emotions with energy-medicine modalities such as Reiki, qigong, craniosacral therapy, and therapeutic touch.

sections.title: Allergic rhinitis — the Holistic Rx
body: In allergic rhinitis (hay fever), the body overreacts to an inhaled substance by making antibodies and releasing IgE and other inflammatory chemicals (like histamines) into the airways. Severity ranges from minor irritation to anaphylaxis; it can be seasonal or perennial (year-round). Symptoms: sneezing, runny nose, itching of the nose/roof of mouth/eyes, swollen eyelids, post-nasal drip, facial pain or pressure, fatigue, dark circles under the eyes, headaches, and loss of hearing, taste, or smell. Diagnosis is by history and physical; RAST blood testing or a scratch test can identify specific allergens, and blood eosinophils can be elevated. Causes are environmental: pollen, mold, smoke, dust mites.

Supplements: raw honey (2 tbsp/day). Stinging nettle (300–500 mg twice daily, herbal or eaten as a green) has antihistamine activity. Butterbur (500 mg/day) reduces mucus. Quercetin (1,000 mg/day). Bromelain (250 mg/day) decreases sinus and nasal swelling. Vitamin C (2,000 mg/day) is an antihistamine and antioxidant. Soil-based probiotics. Others: spirulina (1,000–2,000 mg/day) stops histamine release; Tinospora cordifolia (300 mg three times/day — avoid with autoimmunity, pregnancy, or nursing); Epicor (dried Saccharomyces cerevisiae fermentate, 500 mg/day); astragalus (160 mg twice daily — avoid with autoimmune conditions, lithium, or other immune-suppressing meds); MSM (3,000–5,000 mg/day) reduces allergic/inflammatory responses; eyebright (Euphrasia officinalis, one capsule three times daily, or as a solution — five drops of the tincture in a half-ounce of saline applied to irritated eyes twice daily).

Children's dosing — allergic rhinitis: bromelain (80–320 mg/day), probiotics (2–10 billion CFU/day), mixed carotenoids (1,000–5,000 IU/day), quercetin (200–400 mg divided into two to three doses/day), mixed tocopherols (100–400 IU/day), vitamin C (500–1,000 mg/day), stinging nettle leaf (100–500 mg/day). General allergy: bromelain (200–500 mg/day), flavonoids (200–400 mg divided into two to three daily doses), quercetin (250–500 mg divided into two to three doses/day), vitamin C (500–1,000 mg/day), euphrasia (50–200 mg/day), skullcap (250–500 mg/day), stinging nettle leaf (250–500 mg/day), turmeric (100 mg/day).

Nux vomica for dry, ticklish, scraping sensations with watery discharge, stuffiness, and sneezing on waking, in someone impatient and irritable, light-sensitive, itchy ears, obstructed breathing, craving tobacco/sweets/stimulants. Euphrasia for thick, burning, irritating tears with stinging nasal discharge worse lying down and indoors. Arsenicum album for restlessness, fatigue, anxiety, stuffiness, violent sneezing, and burning copious discharge. Sabadilla for violent sneezing, watery eyes, runny nose, sore throat soothed by warm drinks, headache like the head is shrinking, and feeling cold. Arsenicum iodatum for thick honey-colored nasal discharge followed by three to four days of sneezing and burning inside the nose, plus burning throat, dry skin, anxiety, and irritating cough, worse with warmth. Arundo for itchy nose/ears/roof of mouth with sneezing but no discharge, useful early in hay fever season. Psorinum for feeling cold, bland or burning discharge, wanting to lie down, and breathlessness relieved by raising the arms. Gelsemium for apathy, dizziness, shakiness, nonstop watering and sneezing with puffy heavy eyes. Pulsatilla for tearfulness with yellow eye/nose discharge, nighttime congestion better in open air, worse in a warm room. Silicea for feeling cold, a stuffed nose especially on waking, and tender sinuses, with allergies manifesting as upper respiratory infections and tiredness. Dulcamara for feeling cold after exertion with constant sneezing, stuffy nose, and swollen watery eyes worse outdoors and in damp weather. Sanguinaria for nasal polyps, dry congested nasal membranes, and chronic rhinitis (if with asthma, consider Arsenicum iodatum, Iodum, Arsenicum, Kali iodatum, or Sabadilla). Rhinitis worse with exertion or warmth: Silicea or Pulsatilla. Early hay fever: Arundo and/or Wyethia. Stuffy nose with constant, unrelieved blowing: Lachesis, Psorinum, Naja, Sticta, or Kali bichromicum. The homeopathic combination Sabadil can also help.
Acupressure: LI20, ST20, B2, LI4, SP5, B13, GB20. Others: B10 (fatigue, headaches, swollen eyes), ST36, TW5. Nambudripad Allergy Elimination Technique (NAET) can help rebalance the immune system.

Eucalyptus steam inhalation mixed with ravensara (decongestant), lavender (decreases stress), and peppermint can open the airways. A chamomile balm traps pollen, is anti-inflammatory, and soothes irritated skin. Frankincense boosts the immune system. Others: bergamot, German chamomile, cinnamon, clove bud, helichrysum, juniper needle, lemon, niaouli, peppermint, ravensara, rosemary cineole, rosewood.

sections.title: Sinusitis — the Holistic Rx
body: Sinusitis is inflammation located in the sinuses, causing pain, pressure, nasal congestion, nasal discharge or post-nasal drip, toothache, sore throat, cough, headaches, loss of smell, and fatigue. Causes: infection, obstruction, air-pressure changes, injury, and/or allergies. Diagnosis is by history, physical, and imaging if needed (X-ray, CT, or MRI).

Supplements: a multivitamin twice daily with selenium (100–200 mcg/day), zinc (20–40 mg/day), magnesium (400–600 mg/day), calcium (1,000 mg/day, 1,500 mg/day during menopause), chromium (200 mcg/day), bee propolis (500 mg three times daily), and vitamin E. Grapefruit seed extract (spray four times daily) has antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and anti-aging properties — may slow hepatic metabolism of drugs like statins. Oil of oregano (500 mg four times daily) has antibacterial and antiviral properties. Vitamin C (1,000 mg three times daily) boosts immune function. Garlic (500 mg twice daily) improves immune function but can enhance anticoagulant effects. Echinacea (1,000 mg two to three times daily) fights infection, especially at first sign of symptoms.

Others: nettle for allergies (freeze-dried, 300 mg three times daily); quercetin and bromelain (500 mg/day, between meals); licorice (10–20 drops three times daily); pantothenic acid (500 mg three times daily) with hydrochloric acid (1–2 capsules after protein-based meals) to optimize gut health. N-acetylcysteine (500 mg three times daily) thins mucus to aid sinus drainage. Colloidal silver (spray four times daily for acute sinusitis, twice daily for chronic) and Pelargonium sidoides are helpful. Yin chiao (Chinese herbal formula) three times daily; astaxanthin (4 mg once or twice daily); vitamin B (50 mg twice daily).

For fungal sinusitis and candida overgrowth: garlic or Allimax/Allimed (100% pure allicin), beginning at 720–900 mg three times daily and gradually tapering to 180–450 mg once daily over three months, plus Candex/Candisol (two capsules twice daily on an empty stomach). A combination of antifungal supplements — sodium caprylate, oregano leaf, Pau D'Arco, berberine, grapefruit seed, ginger root, chamomile, biotin, and zinc — can also be used. Pulsatilla for weepiness, pain above the eyes, thick yellow-green discharge with nausea/vomiting worse indoors and better with open cool air, cool compresses, and pressure; right maxillary/frontal sinus involvement with jumpy right-sided facial nerve pain. Bryonia alba for sinus pain worse with any downward head movement. Hepar sulphuris for yellow mucus in later stages, a tender face, sneezing, and pain between the eyes worse with cold dry winds, in someone who feels cold and irritable. Kali bichromicum for fullness and congestion on either side of the nose with stringy thick green/yellow mucus and pain at the roof of the nose. Mercurius solubilis for thick foul-smelling green discharge with a little blood, worse with open air, eating, drinking, and extreme cold or hot, possibly feverish with pain extending to the teeth. Silicea for deep tearing/throbbing pain with an itchy nose tip, worse in the right eye and with light, cold air, movement, noise, and mental concentration. Spigelia for sharp left-sided facial pain relieved by cold compresses or cool water and worse with light, movement, noise, and warmth. Frontal sinuses: GB14, B2, EX HN3. Maxillary sinuses: ST2, SI18. Ethmoidal and sphenoid sinuses: GV16, GV20.

Aromatherapy: eucalyptus oil clears blocked sinuses via steam inhalation, bath, or massage; combine with peppermint, rosemary, and thyme. Tea tree oil fights infection to aid sinus relief. Lavender helps sleep and stimulates the immune system. Others: Canadian balsam, helichrysum, hyssop, lavender, sweet and Spanish marjoram, green or orange myrtle, niaouli, pine, cineole and camphor rosemary, cedarwood, ravensara, cajeput.

sections.title: Tinnitus — the Holistic Rx
body: Tinnitus (ringing in the ears) is a sensation of hearing whistling, ringing, buzzing, sizzling, or other sounds — intermittent or continuous, and may change, stop and go, or get louder and faster. Causes include infections, blockages in the ear, or inner-ear damage; symptoms can improve once the underlying cause is treated. May be accompanied by difficulty concentrating, brain fog, and confusion. Diagnosis by history and physical.

Supplements: B-complex (50 mg/day) supports healthy nerves. Melatonin (1–3 mg/day). Pycnogenol (100–150 mg/day). Bioflavonoids (200–800 mg/day). CoQ10 (100 mg three times daily) may help those low in CoQ10. Magnesium (250 mg twice daily) supports normal hearing. B12 (1,000 mcg/day) supports healthy nerves — get B12 levels tested. Others: Ginkgo biloba (120 mg twice daily of a 24% extract) improves circulation through the inner ear; zinc (90 mg/day with 2–3 mg copper, under a doctor's supervision) may help those with a zinc deficiency.

Kali iodatum for longstanding ringing with no additional symptoms. Calcarea carbonica for crackling or pulsing sensations in the ears, in someone easily cold, fatigued, overwhelmed, and anxious. Lycopodium for roaring/humming like an echo, in someone prone to infections with discharge and digestive issues. Chininum sulphuricum for roaring, buzzing, hissing, or ringing that impairs hearing, possibly with vertigo. Graphites for tinnitus with deafness, skin eruptions, poor concentration, and constipation. sections.title: Vertigo — the Holistic Rx
body: Vertigo is a sensation of dizzy spells in which the environment seems to spin, or you feel like you are spinning. Causes include benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, Meniere's disease, labyrinthitis, or vestibular neuritis (inflammation of the nerve in the inner ear); other causes include injury, medications that damage the ear, stroke, tumors, migraines, or multiple sclerosis. Symptoms: swaying, pulling in one direction, imbalance, and sometimes nausea, headache, sweating, ear fullness, ringing, or hearing loss. Diagnosis by history and physical.

Supplements: Ginkgo biloba (60 mg two or three times daily) increases blood flow to the brain. Cayenne (300 mg twice daily) increases blood flow. CoQ10 (100 mg/day). Turmeric (500 mg twice daily) improves blood flow and lowers inflammation. Ginger root (500 mg twice daily, or 1 cup of tea twice daily). Vinpocetine (15 mg/day) improves inner-ear circulation symptoms. Others: ashwagandha (1,000 mg twice daily) and Panax ginseng (100 mg two to three times daily with 4–7% ginsenosides) improve adrenal function.

For Meniere's disease specifically: magnesium (1,000 mg/day) improves tinnitus and protects the ears from damage; B vitamins (500 mg B1, 250 mg B6, 500 mcg B12) and vitamin C (1,000 mg three times daily) with 250 mg bioflavonoids improve symptoms, as does ginkgo biloba (80–120 mg/day) and fenugreek/chamomile teas. Gelsemium for dizziness with trembling, possibly viral in origin, with drowsiness — also for post-stage-fright dizziness with anxiety, mental dullness, trembling, and visual disturbances. Kali carb for symptoms worse turning, reading, or walking, better in open air. Nux vomica for symptoms worse with flickering bright lights or crowded spaces, possibly with vomiting, nausea, and a hungover feeling, worse in the morning and improving through the day and with lying down. Lachesis for symptoms triggered by feeling congested/claustrophobic, improving with discharge. Phosphoricum acidum for vertigo with headaches and malaise, or following emotional shock. Chininum sulphuricum for hearing loss, ringing in the ears, and vertigo together. Chenopodium anthelminticum for sudden Meniere's disease with hearing loss, liver pain, and migraines. Acupressure: TW17, SI19, TW16. Others: P6, GV20, GV19, GV21, GB20, GB21, Tai Yang, LV2, ST36, K1, GV26, B23, B47, ST9, LV3.

sections.title: Endocrine Health — the Holistic Rx (diet, detox and lifestyle)
body: Lowering inflammation and maintaining a balance of glucose and insulin is key to optimizing endocrine function and supporting weight loss. Add the superfoods of coconut, olives, avocados, fatty fish and other proteins, nuts and seeds, and Himalayan or Celtic sea salt. Eating fat or protein with every meal and limiting carbs helps stabilize blood sugar and improve endocrine function. Increase fiber and vinegar in the diet, as these can stabilize blood sugar. Foods high in chromium can naturally balance blood glucose — broccoli, grass-fed beef, and green beans. Other healing foods are cinnamon, ginger, rosemary, green tea, cranberries, blueberries, lemon balm, fenugreek, holy basil, neem, bay leaves, turmeric, gymnema sylvestre, and bitter melon. Grapefruit, romaine lettuce, celery, curry powder, asparagus, aloe vera, and flounder all help with weight loss. Caffeine can be problematic for those with compromised adrenals, as it may prevent sleep.

After an initial weight loss, some experience a plateau. Insulin resistance keeps insulin levels up, leading to weight gain or the inability to lose weight even when eating the right foods; periods of low insulin achieved through intermittent fasting can help break that cycle. It takes time for the body to adjust to fasting, so give it at least a month, and talk to a primary care provider first to confirm fasting is safe. Plateaus can also reflect increasing muscle mass alongside decreasing fat mass, so track fat mass and lean mass separately along with waist and hip circumference — weight may not change even as measurements do. When a plateau persists, check basal metabolic rate, consider genetic testing, review food intolerances and toxin exposures, increase water intake and sleep, and increase sweating (through exercise or sauna); focus on the foundations of good health and lowering inflammation.
The Four Big S's: lowering stress and improving sleep can help restore hormonal balance across every endocrine condition in this chapter.

sections.title: Adrenal Fatigue — the Holistic Rx
body: The adrenal gland produces and regulates the stress hormone cortisol, along with sex hormones and neurotransmitters that communicate with every organ. Adrenal fatigue is a term applied to a collection of nonspecific symptoms reflecting adrenal dysfunction and resulting nutrient and hormonal imbalance from chronic stress; though not a formal medical diagnosis, it lies on a spectrum between normal function and Addison's disease (when 90 percent of adrenal function is lost). Symptoms include fatigue, trouble waking up, dizziness when standing, irritability and short temper, frequent infections and colds that take time to clear, low body temperature, palpitations, mood disorders, muscle weakness, increased allergies, insomnia, decreased libido, hair loss, headaches, always feeling cold, sugar cravings, low blood pressure, thyroid problems, high energy at bedtime, inflammation, weight gain, muscle tension, light-headedness on standing, chronic pain, PMS symptoms, and a reliance on coffee. Diagnosis can include a blood pressure test for orthostatic hypotension, a pupil contraction test, checking for unstable body temperature, and hormone testing of adrenal hormones, DHEA, adrenal saliva cortisol, and thyroid function.

Supplements: ashwagandha (500 mg once daily); vitamin C (500–3,000 mg daily); B vitamins — B5 (300–1,000 mg per day), B6 (30–100 mg per day), B1 (up to 600 mg per day) — for fatigue and adrenal support; zinc and selenium. Adaptogenic and GABAergic herbs: rhodiola rosea (100–400 mg daily); eleuthero (2–3 g of dried root in a capsule daily); reishi mushroom (3–6 g of dried mushroom in a capsule daily); maca (75–100 mg per day, avoid in pregnancy); phosphatidylserine (100 mg three times per day, or 100–200 mg per day); passionflower (100–200 mg per day); valerian (100–200 mg per day); lemon balm (100–200 mg per day); l-theanine (100–200 mg per day); holy basil (2–3 mg per day) to help recover adrenal function; Siberian, Panax, or Asian ginseng during periods of high stress (100–200 mg, standardized to 4–5% ginsenosides); licorice (50–100 mg per day) for inflammation, especially arthritis or muscle tenderness; tyrosine (500–1,000 mg daily); adrenal glandular (200–500 mg daily); chromium (200–400 µg per day); DHEA (important especially with autoimmune disease such as lupus or Sjogren's, but only under professional guidance); schizandra (20–30 drops of extract, or 2–4 capsules, per day); shatavari (2–4 mg per day).

Homeopathy: Natrum muriaticum for constipation, dry lips and mouth, salt cravings, symptoms worse in hot sun, and a muddy complexion. Argenticum nitricum for tremors, apprehension, and cravings for salt and sweet things. Silicea for lack of stamina and profusely sweating, foul-smelling feet, worse in cold weather. For stress specifically: phosphoric acidum for stress related to grief or bad news; picric acidum for stress from overwork; ignatia for stress following an emotional upset; nux vomica for stress from bad habits (smoking, overeating, overdrinking) or when irritable and overwhelmed.
Acupressure: P6 (to calm and balance), LI4, GB21, LU1, B10, CV17.

Aromatherapy: mix almond oil with clary sage, frankincense, and geranium oils and massage into the skin. Other stress-relieving oils: litsea, orange, and bergamot. For sleep: ylang-ylang, rose, vetiver, and Roman chamomile. Use in massage, a bath, as lotions, or by other methods.

sections.title: Insulin Resistance, Prediabetes, Metabolic Syndrome, and Diabetes — the Holistic Rx
body: Diabetes is a chronic condition marked by abnormally high blood glucose because the body either stops producing insulin or can't use the insulin it produces. Type 1 (juvenile/insulin-dependent) is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system destroys the insulin-producing cells; type 2 occurs when the pancreas can't make enough insulin to keep glucose normal and is made worse by poor food choices. Prediabetes (impaired fasting glucose, impaired glucose tolerance, or insulin resistance) is blood glucose higher than normal but not yet diagnostic of diabetes. Metabolic syndrome (dysmetabolic syndrome X, insulin-resistance syndrome) is a cluster including abdominal obesity, high fasting blood sugar, high blood pressure, low HDL cholesterol, and high triglycerides; about 85 percent of people with diabetes have metabolic syndrome. Signs and symptoms of type 1 include abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, increased urination, increased thirst, fatigue, and absence of menstruation. Type 2 presents as excessive urination and thirst, yeast infections, fatigue, impotence, blurred vision, numbness or burning of the extremities, and poor wound healing. Diagnosis is made by history, physical exam, and blood testing.

Supplements: chromium (600 mcg daily) for insulin sensitivity and blood sugar; cinnamon (2 tsp per day in food, smoothie, or tea); alpha lipoic acid (300–1,200 mg daily) improves insulin sensitivity and reduces/prevents diabetic neuropathy (topical capsaicin up to 4 times per day also helps neuropathy); fiber powder from vegetables and seeds (e.g., PGX, 2–4 capsules before each meal with 8 oz water); berberine (200–300 mg two to four times daily) improves sugar control and retinopathy, avoid in pregnancy; bitter melon; prickly pear; B vitamins (B1, B6, B7, B12); vitamins C, D, K; iodine; zinc; melatonin; choline (reduces fatty liver risk); calcium. For metabolic syndrome/insulin resistance specifically: ginseng; berberine (also restores intestinal barrier function and reduces vascular inflammation — watch for drug interactions); bitter melon; holy basil; spirulina and maca root to raise glutathione and support immune function. Others: gymnema sylvestre (400 mg of a 25% gymnemic acid extract daily) lowers blood sugar; vanadyl sulfate (100–300 mg daily, higher doses under medical supervision) improves glucose tolerance; biotin (9–16 mg daily) for glucose metabolism.

For weight loss: guggul (650 mg twice daily), glucomannan (665 mg before bed), CLA (750 mg twice daily), forskolin (385 mg twice daily), sphaeranthus indicus, garcinia mangostana, green coffee bean extract (400 mg twice daily).
