sections.title: Gut healing — the Holistic Rx (diet and daily habits)
body: Healing the gut is key to nearly every digestive complaint, and eating gut superfoods is essential. Maintain a high-fiber diet, and add fermented veggies and seeds like flax, chia, and hemp to add bulk to stools. Other gut-supportive foods include apple cider vinegar, kombucha, bone broth, healthy fats like coconut oil (a powerful antifungal), wild-caught salmon, almonds, squash, honey, cabbage juice (rich in glutamine), and green leafy and cruciferous veggies (which contain methionine, helpful against H. pylori). Bitter greens — turnip greens, dandelion greens, and mustard greens — help the body produce acid, bile, and enzymes to break down food, and cranberry juice can help prevent H. pylori from adhering to the gut. Eat small meals, filling the stomach only two-thirds of the way, to optimize digestion.

Digestive herbs and herbal teas can aid digestion and decrease bloating and ease acute symptoms: fennel, anise, ginger, peppermint, caraway seeds, cardamom, cloves, lemon balm, spearmint, thyme, celery seed, and basil.

Foods that help eliminate parasites include raw garlic, pumpkin seeds, pomegranates, beets, and carrots. Papaya seeds and papaya extracts (papain) have been helpful in eliminating worms and keeping the intestine in a natural acidic state.

Some patients benefit from a FODMAPs diet, which minimizes poorly absorbed short-chain carbohydrates, including most dairy, corn syrup, wheat products, and vegetables and fruit with a high glucose-to-fructose ratio, such as watermelon and dried fruit.

The four big S's — special considerations: remove the stress from your bowels by creating a bathroom routine and listening to your body instead of ignoring urges. Squatting straightens the anorectal angle and allows for easy passage; using a stool (such as a Squatty Potty) under the feet while seated has the same effect.
sections.source: The Holistic Rx — Madiha Saeed, MD

sections.title: Bloating and gas — the Holistic Rx
body: Bloating is the feeling of gas filling up the stomach or bowels. Digestive disorders, fluid buildup, dehydration, food sensitivities, constipation, hormonal changes, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, infection, cancer, or even bowel obstruction can lead to bloating.

Supplements: gut-healing supplements are optimal for relieving bloating, including probiotics, digestive enzymes, and even activated charcoal tablets (which help absorb toxins and gases) and chlorophyll, taken with each meal.

Homeopathy: Carbo vegetabilis helps with bloating and belching. Lycopodium is useful for passing gas when constipation is also present, especially when eating onions or garlic. Dioscorea is helpful for gas in the presence of diarrhea and abdominal pain that is better by bending backward. Ignatia is a remedy for bloating of the abdomen after grief. Natrum carbonicum helps those who have trouble digesting foods, associated with heartburn, ulcers, and dairy-induced gas and diarrhea — they crave sweets and potatoes. Thuja is indicated for abdominal bloating, chronic diarrhea, and rumbling of the bowels accompanied by lots of gas. Others that can be used are Ambra grisea, Arnica montana, Aurum muriaticum, folliculinum, Phosphoricum acidum, and sulphur.
Acupressure: ST36, SP6, LV3. Others: ST25, CV6, ST37, ST41, LI4.
Aromatherapy: angelica, cardamom, Roman chamomile, fennel, ginger, lemon, peppermint, and rosemary cineole can help with bloating.
sections.source: The Holistic Rx — Madiha Saeed, MD

sections.title: Candidiasis — the Holistic Rx
body: Candida albicans is one of the most common types of yeast infection, found in the vagina, digestive system, mucous membranes, and skin. Candida can overgrow when the immune system isn't working properly; broad-spectrum antibiotics, birth control pills, oral corticosteroids, a high-sugar diet, chronic anxiety and other negative emotions, cancer treatments, and diabetes can trigger candidal overgrowth. Symptoms include fatigue, brain fog, sinus issues, bloating, gas, abdominal and joint pain and other digestive issues, bad breath, sleep and mood disorders, sugar cravings, blood sugar and hormonal imbalances, muscle aches, allergies/sinus issues, loss of sex drive, foggy thinking, recurring infections (especially urinary tract and vaginal), oral thrush, skin and nail fungal infections, food intolerances, and sensitivity to smells, sounds, or light.

Supplements: focus on healing the gut and supporting the liver, with probiotics and milk thistle. Natural antifungals: oil of oregano (300–500 mg three times per day with meals, minimum sixty days), berberine, caprylic acid (1,000 mg three times per day), hemicelluloses. Spleen support: licorice, gentian (250 mg at the beginning of each meal), coptis, gardenia, skullcap, ginseng. Others: selenium (decreases oxidative stress), garlic (500–1,000 mg of aged garlic twice daily, or two cloves daily), grapefruit seed extract (200 mg two to three times daily), vitamin C (1,000 mg twice per day), pau d'arco tea, S. boulardii (5–15 billion CFU two to four times per day for sixty days), and activated charcoal (two to four capsules per day at bedtime for sixty days; may deplete magnesium, so replace it). Start any anti-candidal agent at a low dose and increase very gradually to reduce symptoms of candidal die-off reaction.

Children: probiotics, baking soda (1/4 tsp gargled or swallowed in water or formula four times daily), garlic paste applied topically twice daily, lemon juice (1 tbsp diluted in 8 oz of water, applied topically, gargled, or swallowed twice daily), lemongrass infusion (applied topically or gargled twice daily), a GI-probiotic, black walnut hull tincture (1:1 ratio, one drop per ten pounds of body weight in a glass of water three times daily), caprylic acid (250–500 mg daily), garlic (one to three cloves daily), olive leaf (250–1,000 mg daily). For fungal overgrowth generally: oregano, garlic, caprylic acid, grapeseed extract, probiotics, olive leaf extract.

Homeopathy: Candida albicans (look for 30C). Sepia — yeast infection with yellowish discharge, bearing-down sensation, chronic constipation, itching of the skin, fatigue, but improved by exercise and sunlight; irritable/moody, often chilly but worse in a warm room with limited circulation. Pulsatilla — cries easily, irritable and indifferent; itching or red skin on the chest and abdomen; discharge thick and yellowish-green with vulvar swelling; better in open air, worse lying down, heat, warm rooms. Calcarea carbonica — constipated, overweight, craves sweet and salty; yeast infections thick, creamy yellow, with burning and itching; catches colds easily; coldness of the top of the head and legs with sweating (especially the back of the head) on minimal exertion. Sulphur — burning or redness anywhere on the body (face, ears, rectum, nose, vagina); warm patient, worse from heat, burning soles at night, diarrhea at 5:00 a.m. Graphites — thick, cracked skin at the corners of the mouth or heels. Kreosotum — irritating discharge causing swelling or itching, bad odor, redness, rawness, and pain on urination. Borax — diarrhea with bleeding oral mucosa, rash, discharge sticky and runny like egg whites. Belladonna — bright red, painful inflamed skin, not raw or oozing; irritable. Chamomilla — irritability and diaper rash. Arsenicum album — itchy, burning rashes with anxiety.
Acupressure: SP9, LI4, LV3.

Aromatherapy: essential oils that act as antifungals include oregano, clove, myrrh, melaleuca, and thyme. Lavender oil can help inhibit candida growth. Peppermint oil can relieve intestinal cramping. Others: cedarwood, eucalyptus globulus, geranium, helichrysum, lavandin, lemon, manuka, rosemary verbenone, rosewood, and tea tree.

sections.title: Constipation — the Holistic Rx
body: Constipation is hardened feces with difficulty emptying the bowels; it is important to find the root cause. Causes may relate to lifestyle, dehydration, gut problems, poor bathroom and sleep habits, magnesium deficiency, and medications (antidepressants, antacids, blood pressure medications, painkillers); it can also be associated with diabetes, thyroid disease, hormonal problems and other chronic illnesses, older age, poor sleep, jet lag, and travel. It is diagnosed by history and physical.

Supplements: cod liver oil. Psyllium (5 g psyllium husk twice daily). Flax seed oil or flax seeds (1–2 tbsp daily). Pectin. Aloe vera juice. Others: senna (one to four pills per day), cascara sagrada (250 mg, or 2.5 ml of tincture, two to three times daily for acute constipation), triphala. Children: magnesium (100–250 mg daily), probiotics, castor oil rubbed clockwise on the abdomen, zinc (20–40 mg daily).

Homeopathy: Nux vomica — great urge to defecate but nothing passes, or incomplete defecation; good for those who study hard or are sedentary, elderly, or laxative-dependent; cold, irritable, overstressed. Bryonia — large, dry, hard stools with headaches, congestion, and burning in the rectum after stooling; thirsty and irritable; works well in the elderly. Alumina — no desire to defecate until the rectum is completely full; stools may feel as if they accumulate under the left rib area; even soft stools are hard to pass; indicated in the elderly, who may have memory issues. Natrum muriaticum — hard, crumbly stools every second day or longer; rectum dry and painful; strong thirst for water and salt; possible depression. Sulphur — constipation alternating with diarrhea, stools every two to four days, dark, hard, and large with incomplete defecation, hemorrhoids and anal fissure; burning rectum; strong thirst for ice-cold drinks. Silicea — small, hard stools covered with mucus, sore anus, head sweats, and the feeling of the stool sliding back in; cold and thin patients. Opium — no desire to defecate for days, poor appetite, alert to the slightest noise, wakeful at night and drowsy by day. Graphites — anal fissure or hemorrhoids, no desire to stool for days, then colicky pain and passage of stool covered in white mucus; bowels may ache afterward. Aesculus — fullness, crawling sensation in the anus, rectum hot and dry, feels full of spikes; sensation of a knife opening the bowels. Nitric acidium — splinter-like pain lasting hours after stooling, burning, tearing, itching. Plumbum metallicum — sharp colicky pains with little outcome; stools hard, dry, and black. Lycopodium — relieves constipation and gas when there's no desire to pass a stool and, when passed, it's painful and worse between 4:00 and 8:00 p.m.; craves sweets; improves with warm drinks. Ammonium muriaticum — burning sensation in the anus and rectum; after much straining, crumbly, hard, dry stools. Magnesia muriatica — dry, hard stools that crumble around the anus. Causticum — older individuals prone to ankylosis with ineffectual urge to stool. Hydrastis canadensis — constipated stools covered with mucus, no desire to defecate; very effective in pregnant women, children, and chronic laxative users. Raphanus niger — belly distension and gas at the left upper abdomen, distended and painful, improves with passing gas. Calcarea carbonica — feels overwhelmed, chronically constipated, hands and feet cold and clammy. Sepia — constipation with hormonal issues, heavy sensation in the rectum and lower abdomen.
Acupressure: LV3, LI4, LI11, ST36, CV12.

Aromatherapy: carrot seed, orange, and fennel soothe the digestive system; spearmint soothes digestion. Others: black pepper, marjoram, grapefruit, ginger, mandarin, bergamot, rosemary cineole, jasmine, lavender, rose, pine, sandalwood, and ylang-ylang.

Other recommendations: never repress the urge to defecate — holding back trains the bowels to misbehave and can lead to chronic, even lifelong, constipation. It is possible to retrain the bowels: sit on the toilet at the same time every day, even without an urge — early morning or right after exercise are usually good times. Do not strain (it only creates hemorrhoids or varicose veins); instead breathe deeply using the abdominal muscles and try to relax.
sections.source: The Holistic Rx — Madiha Saeed, MD

sections.title: Diarrhea — the Holistic Rx
body: Diarrhea increases the frequency, volume, and wateriness of stool and may be due to a virus or infection; chronic diarrhea (more than four weeks) can signal another bowel issue like inflammatory bowel disease or irritable bowel syndrome. Other causes include reactions to medications, sensitivities to foods or artificial sweeteners, thyroid problems, diabetes, and other chronic illnesses. Other symptoms include bloating, nausea, vomiting, and an urgent need to pass a bowel movement. Diagnosis is made by history and physical.

Supplements: gut-healing supplements — probiotics, digestive enzymes, glutamine, and aloe vera juice (1/2 cup three times daily). Raw sprouted fiber from flax and chia seeds (3 tbsp daily). Others: ginger (500 mg in capsule), goldenseal (300 mg capsule four times per day), oregano oil (500 mg capsule four times per day) as an antimicrobial, and astragalus (500–1,000 mg two to three times per day, not to be taken with a fever). Children: probiotics, zinc (10–20 mg daily), glutamine (0.3 g/kg daily), calcium (200–500 mg daily), fiber (5–15 g three times per day with plenty of water), berberine (400 mg daily), digestive enzymes, colostrum, lauricidin (1/4 tsp three times daily, increasing as needed for normal stool consistency), echinacea, aloe extracts, fatty acids.

Homeopathy: Aconite — sudden diarrhea after cold wind, shock, or summer overheating; distended abdomen, better after passing a stool. Aloe socotrina — morning violent diarrhea with abdominal rumbling, then gushing stools after an anger outburst or food sensitivity exposure; stools yellowish-green and mucus-filled; worse after meals with excessive gas. Arsenicum album — exhausting diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting; scant, odorless stool, may have blood and burn the anus; better with sips of hot drinks, worse with cold drinks, foods, and overripe fruit. Podophyllum — offensive diarrhea with a batter-like consistency, color of pea soup; gas with morning urgency. Phosphoric acidium — profuse, painless watery stools with bits of food, after emotional shock or overeating; better after defecation. Sulphur — burning, explosive, foul-smelling diarrhea that forces a person out of bed at 5:00 a.m., hemorrhoids present, anus red and excoriated, craves cold liquids. Veratrum — profuse, painful, rice-water diarrhea with vomiting, cold sweats, craving ice water. China — stools like chopped egg, excessive gas, chronic spasms, exhaustion and weakness following diarrhea; very irritable; worse with summer chills or eating fruit. Colocynth — excessive diarrhea brought on by anger, with gripping pain relieved by doubling up, pressure, and heat; stools yellowish, thin, and frothy. Dulcamara — slimy, green or yellow stool, may have blood, brought on by damp weather or getting cold after exertion. Pulsatilla — stools that don't look alike, worse at night, in a warm room, from cold drinks, onions, and rich fatty foods; better in open air. Argenticum nitricum — painless emotional or nervous diarrhea with bloating and gastric burning, can follow sugar ingestion. Chamomilla — yellow-green diarrhea in teething infants. Ipecacuanha — nausea with diarrhea. Mercurius solubilis — spasmodic, burning, or bloody diarrhea with extreme sweating. Phosphorus — diarrhea in anxious people who crave cold liquids. Antimonium crudum — stools partly solid, partly liquid; thick white-coated tongue; overweight, with impetigo and hyperkeratosis. Natrum sulphuricum — violent, watery diarrhea after meals with a yellow/greenish coated tongue; overweight, may have depression, cold-sensitive. Paratyphoidinum — chronic diarrhea.
Acupressure: LI4, LI11, ST36, SP6, SP4, SP16 (abdominal cramps), CV6 (with gas). Others: SP15, SP4, LV3.

Aromatherapy: essential oils with antispasmodic properties can relieve abdominal cramps — neroli, mandarin, cypress, eucalyptus, fennel, chamomile, peppermint, black pepper, and ginger. Others: lemon balm, lavender, cedarwood, cinnamon, clove (bud), geranium, ginger, marjoram, niaouli, nutmeg, sandalwood, and spearmint.

sections.title: Diverticulosis — the Holistic Rx
body: Diverticulosis is a condition in which small bulging pouches develop in the digestive tract; it is common in those over forty. It is asymptomatic unless the diverticula become inflamed and infected (diverticulitis), which can cause abdominal pain, nausea, alternating diarrhea and constipation, and fever. Diagnosis is made with lab tests or imaging.

Supplements: gut-healing supplements are important — probiotics, digestive enzymes, slippery elm (500 mg three times per day), aloe vera juice or powder (during an attack take 12–16 oz of aloe juice per day), licorice root (100–300 mg per day), and psyllium fiber to prevent constipation. Others: colloidal silver (1 tsp four times daily) and boswellia (500 mg three times per day).

Homeopathy: Nitricum acidum — beneficial for diverticulosis in the rectosigmoid area. Belladonna — sudden abdominal pain and cramping with constipation, worse with motion, better with firm pressure. Bryonia — left-sided sharp abdominal pain, worse with movement, relieved with heat; accompanied by constipation and vomiting. Colocynthis — cramping, sharp pain that improves with pressure, accompanied by diarrhea and restlessness. Arsenicum album — burning pain, anxious and restless, relieved by a warm environment. Ignatia amara — digestive spasms associated with emotional stress. Magnesia phosphorica — abdominal cramping that worsens with pressure and is relieved by warmth. Nux vomica — cramping pain, especially in a cold-sensitive, irritable person.
Acupressure: CV4, SP4, P6, ST36, CV6 (gas and diarrhea), SP16 (abdominal cramps), LI11 (overall gut health).

Aromatherapy: essential oils with an antispasmodic effect that help relax the abdomen include German chamomile, lavender, geranium, ginger, juniper (berry), Melissa, myrrh, niaouli, bitter orange, peppermint, rosemary, and marjoram.
sections.source: The Holistic Rx — Madiha Saeed, MD

sections.title: Gallstones — the Holistic Rx
body: Gallstones are tiny pieces of solid matter in the gallbladder, formed when cholesterol, calcium, and other particles in bile bind together. Symptoms vary depending on where the gallstone is located, but an attack can bring pain, nausea, and upper-right-sided abdominal pain that can radiate under the right shoulder blade or into the back. Diagnosis is made by imaging such as ultrasound or CT, or more specialized imaging.

Supplements: supplements can improve liver health and regulate the production and use of cholesterol. Turmeric, milk thistle (150 mg twice daily), dandelion root (500 mg with meals). Others: activated charcoal helps bind and remove toxins; vitamin C (1–3 g daily) can decrease gallstone formation; vitamin E (200–400 IU per day); lipase enzymes (two capsules with meals to improve fat digestion); bile salts or ox bile (500–1,000 mg with meals) to improve fat breakdown and gallbladder function; phosphatidylcholine (100 mg two or three times per day) can help smooth the bile and decrease stone formation; barberry helps cleanse the gallbladder and liver; L-methionine (1 g per day).
Homeopathy: Berberis 6C. China — for those who are oversensitive and always cold.
Acupressure: for gallbladder health, LV3. Others: GB34, P6, LI4, LV14, CV14, ST36, and Zhigou (TH6).
Aromatherapy: rosemary oil can help reduce inflammation and can be massaged over the gallbladder area twice daily.
sections.source: The Holistic Rx — Madiha Saeed, MD

sections.title: GERD — the Holistic Rx
body: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and acid reflux symptoms include heartburn, dry mouth, bitter taste in mouth, regurgitation of acid or food, bad breath, gum irritation, belching after meals, bloating one to two hours after meals, feeling full easily, low appetite, difficulty swallowing, chronic constipation, undigested food in stool, rectal itching, anemia, waking up choking, nausea, hiccups, discomfort lying down or bending over, hoarseness, chronic throat irritation, dry and peeling nails, sour taste in mouth, coughing at night, and soreness. As it progresses it can lead to blood in vomit, black stools, and unexpected weight loss. Acid reflux can result from not enough stomach acid, drugs like NSAIDs, birth control pills, muscle relaxers, nitroglycerine, steroids, tight clothing, pregnancy, being overweight or obese, hiatal hernia, stress, large meals, food sensitivities, and excessive exercise.

Supplements: probiotics, digestive enzymes, and HCl with pepsin, L-glutamine, and so on. Others to soothe the gut lining: licorice root (DGL) (one or two 400 mg tablets twenty minutes before each meal). Aloe vera juice (1/2 cup twice a day) helps soothe internal inflammation. D-limonene (1,000 mg per day for ten doses as needed). Slippery elm (300 mg daily, or 1 tsp/3 ml tincture three times per day). Others include chamomile tea, melatonin (6 mg at bedtime), orange peel extract (one capsule of 98.5% D-limonene extract every other day for twenty-one days), vitamin C, peppermint oil, capsaicin, and meadowsweet (1 cup of tea with 1–2 tsp). For Barrett's esophagus: the above can also be used, along with quercetin (500–6,000 mg daily) to protect esophageal tissue, antioxidants like vitamin C (1,000 mg daily), vitamin E, selenium (200–400 mcg per day), NAC (1,000–2,000 mg) and lipoic acid, and other gut-healing herbs like marshmallow, gamma oryzanol, and/or turmeric. Children: apple cider vinegar (1/4 tsp before meals), DGL (300 mg three times daily).

Homeopathy: Carbo vegetabilis — bloating and belching/gas after eating, light burning sensation in the stomach radiating to the back; cold, pale, craves fresh air, feels better with cool things. Nux vomica — heartburn about a half hour after eating with constipation, brought on by excessive food, alcohol, and stress/work; irritable and oversensitive. Pulsatilla — heartburn worse after rich, fatty food, worse in a warm room, better in fresh air; attack begins two hours after eating with pressure under the breastbone, bad taste, nausea, weepiness, desire for comfort, headaches around the eyes. Arsenicum album — heartburn after eating with a stone-weight sensation in the stomach; anxious, restless, vomits or retches until exhausted; better sipping warm water and sitting up, worse in the morning. Bryonia — heartburn after eating, heavy-stone feeling, nausea, faintness, mouth filling with bitter fluid; relieved lying on the back, worse with pressure or slightest movement. China — stomach full of air, sluggish and apathetic, worse at night, not relieved by belching, recent fluid loss (blood, sweat, semen), chopped-egg stool appearance. Anacardium — indigestion one to two hours after meals, foul mouth taste, stomach feels blocked, improves with eating again, worse with cold drinks; forgetful; can be used if peptic ulcer is suspected. Argenticum nitricum — indigestion after sweet foods, alternating constipation and diarrhea, belching, fluttery stomach; suspected peptic ulcer. Sepia — heartburn improved by lying on the right side and by eating; sudden empty stomach feeling, sour mouth taste, bloating, liver tenderness, nausea from smelling food; craves pickles. Lycopodium — gas and bloating, feels full quickly, not improved by belching; anxiety, lack of confidence, constipation, worse in tight clothes, late afternoon/evening; improves with warm fluids; suspected peptic ulcer. Phosphorus — burning chest sensations relieved by ice-cold water but followed by vomiting and nausea; suspected peptic ulcer. Graphites — burning hunger pains relieved by food or hot drinks like milk, nausea after sweets; used for peptic ulcers. Kali bichromium — nausea and vomiting after beer, pain in a particular spot, distended stomach; used for peptic ulcers. Sulphur — diarrhea, burning pain, belching improved by ice-cold drinks. Natrum carbonicum — trouble digesting most foods. Antimonium crudum — pain in the pit of the stomach with overeating, white thick milky tongue, hyperkeratosis and impetigo eruptions. Others: robinia (excess acid, worse at night, frontal and temporal headache), sulphuricum acidum (stomach pain after alcohol and from hiatal hernia, ulcerative stomatitis), asa foetida (aerophagia), nux moschata (extreme flatulence), chelidonium majus (pain in the hepatobiliary region radiating to the inferior angle of the right scapula), hydrastis canadensis (hepatobiliary pain in a thin, tired, constipated person), ignatia (paradoxical cramps and burning worse around 11:00 a.m., improved by entertainment), lachesis (heartburn with PMS, hemorrhoids, hot flashes, and rectal bleeding, after excessive alcohol and during menopause), and thuja occidentalis (gas, colonic distention worse two to three hours after meals, relieved by heat; overweight, cold-sensitive, phobia-prone).
Acupressure: HP6, ST36, CV12, SP4. For gastritis: ST21, ST36, SP4, B21, CV12.

Aromatherapy: a peppermint and ginger massage — combining sunflower oil carrier with peppermint essential oil, ginger essential oil, and dill oil — can relieve reflux symptoms. Antispasmodic, calming, warming oils like cardamom, coriander, and mandarin can relieve indigestion. Others: cedarwood, Roman chamomile, lemon, sandalwood, anise, basil linalool, bergamot, fennel, lavender, mandarin, marjoram, rosemary cineole, spearmint, and thyme linalool. Use aromatherapy at least two hours apart from eating and exercise.

Other recommendations: drink more water, but not with meals; stay upright after meals; stay upright after large meals and elevate the head of the bed by six inches; avoid tight-fitting clothing around the middle. Heel drops can help reset a hiatal hernia — standing, take a gulp of water and come up on your tiptoes, then, as you swallow, drop your heels to the ground.

sections.title: Hemorrhoids — the Holistic Rx
body: Hemorrhoids are rectal or anal veins that become painful and swollen. There are two types: internal (inside the anus or lower rectum) and external (outside the anal opening). Symptoms include anal pain and itching, painful bowel movements, bright red blood on stool/toilet paper/in the bowel, and harder, tender lumps near the anus. Diagnosis is by history and physical exam; a doctor may use an anoscope or sigmoidoscope to look inside the anal canal.

Supplements: fiber, like psyllium husk. Pycnogenol (100 mg twice daily) for acute hemorrhoids. Horse chestnut (100 mg daily) improves circulation and vascular tone. Witch hazel reduces inflammation and pain. Others: butcher's broom treats chronic venous insufficiency; diosmin (1,000–3,000 mg per day in divided doses for one week for acute issues, then 1,000 mg per day in divided doses for at least two to three months) reduces symptoms of chronic or recurrent hemorrhoids; collinsonia (500 mg three times a day) reduces swelling; bioflavonoid complex (1,000 mg two or three times daily) reduces swelling and prevents bleeding; bilberry; vitamin E (400–800 IU of alpha and mixed tocopherol daily). For temporary relief of pain and itching, use as a topical: cocoa butter, zinc oxide, olive oil, or calendula gel. Salves: vitamin E oil, comfrey, calendula ointment, or goldenseal salve gently applied to the anus with fingers; witch hazel is also soothing.

sections.title: Inflammatory bowel disease — the Holistic Rx
body: Inflammatory bowel disease is chronic inflammation of all or part of the digestive tract; types include Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. Symptoms include pain, fatigue, diarrhea, weight loss, fever, nausea and vomiting, floating stools, anemia, rectal bleeding, and joint pain. Ulcerative colitis causes open sores or ulcers in the innermost layer of the large intestine and rectum; Crohn's disease can occur anywhere in the digestive tract, often in patches surrounded by healthy tissue. Diagnosis is made by blood tests, colonoscopy and sigmoidoscopy with possible biopsy, barium enema, and other imaging.

Supplements: focus on gut-healing supplements plus calcium and a multivitamin with antioxidants, zinc, vitamin C (500 mg), vitamin E (400 IU of mixed tocopherols and tocotrienols), curcumin, bromelain (2,000–3,000 mg per day), and slippery elm. Others: aloe vera, DGL (300 mg before meals), enzymes (one to two capsules with each meal), glutamine (1–3 g three times daily on an empty stomach), phosphatidylcholine and IgA supplements, marshmallow, cat's claw (250 mg per day), and boswellia (can help in Crohn's, but should not be taken more than eight weeks straight).

Children — Crohn's disease: fish oil (EPA/DHA 3 g daily), probiotics, vitamin D (1,000–5,000 IU daily), NAC (3–6 g daily), glutamine (5,000 mg daily), bromelain (250–1,000 mg daily), butyrate (4 g daily), fiber, L-carnitine (500–2,000 mg daily), turmeric standardized extract (400–600 mg daily). Ulcerative colitis: probiotics, fish oil (3 g EPA/DHA daily), vitamin D (1,000–4,000 IU daily), bromelain (250–1,000 mg daily), butyrate (500–1,000 mg daily), vitamin C (500–2,000 mg daily), curcumin (500–1,000 mg daily).

Aromatherapy: frankincense improves circulation and digestive health. Chamomile, lavender, and lemongrass oils relieve pain. Ginger, peppermint, and fennel relieve inflammation.

sections.title: Irritable bowel syndrome — the Holistic Rx
body: Irritable bowel syndrome leads to diarrhea, constipation, and pain after bowel movements, mucus in the stool, an immediate need to go to the bathroom on waking and during or after meals, and a feeling of incomplete emptying due to faster or slower intestinal contractions.

Children: digestive enzymes, probiotics, fiber, melatonin (3 mg daily), tryptophan (1–5 g daily), peppermint oil (one enteric-coated capsule three times daily), artichoke leaf extract with 13–18% caffeoylquinic acid (200–500 mg daily).

sections.title: Intestinal parasites — the Holistic Rx
body: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in a host and causes disease and illness. Parasites can enter the system from contaminated food or water; those with leaky gut or a weakened immune system are more prone to infection. Symptoms come in waves but never fully go away: night sweats, fatigue, allergies, digestive issues, anal itching, unexpectedly high white blood cell count, skin rashes (eczema, psoriasis, rosacea, hives, or unexplained rash), trouble falling asleep, waking multiple times at night, teeth grinding, muscle aches, never feeling satisfied after eating, and iron-deficiency anemia. Suspect parasites when symptoms worsen after camping or travel where contaminated water may have been consumed. A comprehensive stool test can help detect parasites, but a negative test isn't always definitive.

Supplements: before starting a parasite cleanse, make sure you have daily regular bowel movements. Black walnut (250 mg three times daily). Wormwood (200 mg three times daily). Oregano oil (500 mg four times daily) has antiparasitic effects. Grapefruit seed extract (as directed). Clove oil (500 mg four times daily). Ginger root (500 mg four times daily). Others: coptis (gold thread) (200 mg three times daily), a Chinese antiparasitic herb, and goldenseal (300 mg four times daily) to fight gut and digestive tract infections. Other helpful herbs: aloe, anise, barberry, cashew, curled mint, Oregon grape, papaya, pomegranate, pumpkin, sweet basil, thyme, and turmeric.

sections.title: Peptic ulcer disease — the Holistic Rx
body: Peptic ulcers are sores on the lining of the esophagus, stomach, or small intestine. Symptoms include pain that can be felt anywhere, worse when the stomach is empty and flaring up at night; the pain can be temporarily relieved by food or acid-blocking medication. Diagnosis is made via lab and imaging tests. About 70 percent of ulcers are due to H. pylori overgrowth; others are due to NSAIDs that damage the digestive lining.

Supplements (used alongside pharmaceutical therapy): continue to focus on gut-healing supplements, like probiotics and L-glutamine. Chamomile (1 cup four times daily) soothes the nerves and heals ulcers. Vitamin E (400 IU of mixed tocopherols daily) protects against and helps destroy H. pylori. Grapefruit seed extract (ten drops three times daily) has strong antimicrobial action. Zinc (75 mg twice daily) heals the lining and fights bacteria. Additional help for H. pylori: vitamin C (500 mg twice daily) helps eradicate infection and heal tissue; licorice root (500 mg before meals) may help stop H. pylori and heal the gut lining; aloe vera (500 mg two to three times daily) helps fight H. pylori; mastic gum (500 mg two to three times per day for sixty days); S. boulardii (5–15 billion CFU two to four times per day for sixty days). Supportive treatment: cabbage juice (4 oz daily for twenty-eight days). Others: citrus seed extract, goldenseal, activated charcoal, and gamma oryzanol. Sano-Gastril, comfrey, and calendula have also been shown to help heal ulcers. Children: juiced cabbage daily (may interact with cancer therapies), glutamine (500 mg twice daily).

Graphites — burning hunger pains relieved by food or hot drinks like milk, nausea after sweets; used for peptic ulcers. Kali bichromium — nausea and vomiting after beer, pain in a particular spot, distended stomach with cessation of digestion; used for peptic ulcers. Sulphur — diarrhea, burning pain, belching improved by ice-cold drinks. sections.title: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth — the Holistic Rx
body: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) is a condition where bacteria grow in the wrong place — normally the colon has far more bacteria than the small intestine. When bacteria overgrow in the small intestine, it can promote intestinal permeability. Symptoms include difficulty digesting meals, gas, bloating and abdominal distension (especially after meals or most of the time), odorous loose stools, abdominal pain, signs of leaky gut or chronic disease, or a diagnosed B12 and iron deficiency. Causes include antibiotic use, acid-suppressing medication, food poisoning, and low stomach acid, among others. SIBO can be confirmed with a lactulose hydrogen and methane breath test that detects excessive gas generated by overgrowing bacteria fermenting dietary sugars and starches; retest with another breath test within two weeks of finishing SIBO treatment.

Supplements: wormwood. Berberine-containing botanicals (like Berberis vulgaris). Caprylic acid. Grapefruit and other citrus seed extracts. Black walnut. Oil of oregano (150 mg, two capsules, three times per day for sixty days). For methane-producing bacteria, add garlic extract (two capsules, three times per day for sixty days). Others: goldenseal. Supportive treatment: peppermint tea (two to three cups per day). If regrowth occurs: prophylactic use of betaine with pepsin, low-dose naltrexone, low-dose erythromycin; Bifidobacterium lactis and Lactobacillus rhamnosus can help prevent recurrence.
Homeopathy, acupressure, and aromatherapy (oregano, thyme, and sage) are similar to the remedies used for bloating and other specific symptoms.

sections.title: Dysmenorrhea (painful periods) and endometriosis — the Holistic Rx
body: A woman's reproductive system is often the first system to show signs the body is out of balance — irregular periods and pelvic pain are frequent early signals. Managing glucose effectively, healing the gut, and taming toxins lowers gynecologic problems and helps balance hormone levels. With heavy or irregular bleeding, focus on high-iron foods along with vitamin C, which increases iron absorption and triggers ovulation; foods rich in vitamin E, folate, and zinc also optimize reproductive health. The Four Big S's — staying away from stress, getting good sleep, having healthy social relationships, and cultivating a spiritual practice — all help lower cortisol and balance hormones.

Painful periods can occur due to numerous issues, including hormonal imbalances and endometriosis. Diagnosis is via history and examination, along with imaging like ultrasound or more invasive techniques. Endometriosis is when uterine tissue lands on pelvic tissue, leading to dysmenorrhea, painful stools, and painful sexual intercourse.

Supplements: vitex (chasteberry) (400 mg twice daily) balances hormones — don't take with oral contraceptive pills. Fish oil (1,000 mg daily); gamma-linoleic acid from evening primrose oil or borage oil (300 mg) can also help. B complex (50 mg daily). Natural progesterone cream (1/4 tsp days 6 through 26 of the cycle, stopping after the third month of pregnancy or the week of your menses) balances out estrogen. Milk thistle (150 mg twice daily). Others: indole-3-carbinol (300 mg daily) helps the liver detoxify estrogen; dandelion root (300–500 mg with each meal) helps liver detoxification; vitamin E (400 IU twice daily) helps with inflammation and estrogen metabolism; D-glucarate (500 mg daily) assists the liver in estrogen breakdown. Vitamin C (6–10 g per day), beta-carotene (50,000 IU per day), selenium (200–400 mcg per day), and lipotropics (1,000 mg choline and 1,000 mg methionine or cysteine three times per day) can also be tried.

Lachesis — anger, jealousy, suspicion; menstrual cramps with large purple clots and frequent PMS. Lilium tigrinum — hypersensitivity of the vulva. Magnesia phosphorica — spasmodic pelvic pain, cramping, and bloating soothed by heat, pressure, and movement; worse in cold air; membranes found in the flow. Murex — painful, heavy periods with clots. Nux vomica — prolonged, early periods with constipation, irritability, chilliness, and exhaustion; pain is spasmodic. Dysmenorrhea — clary sage helps balance hormones and has been shown to reduce symptoms of endometriosis; angelica, chamomile, fennel, ginger, lavender, frankincense, and sandalwood can help reduce inflammation and support healing. sections.title: Uterine fibroids — the Holistic Rx
body: Fibroids are uterine growths of connective tissue that can lead to heavy, prolonged periods and pelvic pain. Assessment is via history and examination/pelvic exam and imaging (ultrasound, MRI, hysterosalpingography, and/or hysteroscopy). Healing the underlying root cause and balancing hormones are key to improving symptoms.

Supplements: vitex (chasteberry) (400 mg twice daily) balances the estrogen/progesterone ratio — do not use with a birth control pill. Others: natural progesterone cream (1/4 tsp, days 6–26 of the cycle; if pregnant, stop after the third month) helps balance low progesterone; antioxidants, N-acetylcysteine, and other detoxification supplements (1,200 mg/day), like indole-3-carbinol (300 mg daily), dandelion root (Taraxacum officinale) (300–500 mg with meals, three times a day), and D-glucarate (500 mg daily). Vitamin E (400 IU twice daily) helps with estrogen metabolism and inflammation. Other herbal therapies: Scudder's, Fraxinus ceanothus, Turska's, and specific herbal formulas for specific symptoms (menorrhagia, dysmenorrhea, etc.). Warm castor oil packs placed on the abdomen can be effective to shrink fibroids and relieve pain, along with ginger compresses. Heavy bleeding can be controlled with uterine-toning herbs like black cohosh, red raspberry, and false unicorn root, or astringent herbs like cinnamon, yarrow, beth root, and lady's mantle, or oxytocic herbs like shepherd's purse — often found in combinations. The tonic and astringent herbs can be used twice a day for two weeks before the period, then shepherd's purse is added once bleeding begins; a combination of all three herbs can be taken every thirty minutes for up to six doses. Pain and cramping can be helped with herbs like black cohosh, boswellia, ginger, turmeric, cayenne, cramp bark, and mitchella repens, and enzymes like neprinol, bromelain, and wobenzym. B complex (50 mg daily, as B vitamins are involved in estrogen metabolism) and milk thistle (150 mg twice daily) help balance hormones and detox the liver.

Phosphorus — bright red blood with clotting, craves ice-cold drinks. Sabina — lower back and sacral pain reaching to the pubic bones, with heavy uterine bleeding and clots. Silicea — bleeding between periods, flow heavier than usual, constantly cold. Sepia — irritable, wants to be left alone, craves salty, sour, and sweet foods; uterus feels like it will fall out with a bearing-down sensation. Sulphur — fibroids in women who overheat easily, desire a cool environment, strong craving for ice-cold drinks. Kali iodatum — uterus feels squeezed during periods. Calcarea iodatum — small fibroids with yellow, profuse vaginal discharge. Thlaspi — continuous bleeding.

Aromatherapy: frankincense, thyme, and clary sage can help. Two drops of frankincense oil, twice daily, on the roof of the mouth, and two drops of the other oils rubbed over the lower abdomen a couple of times a day, can help balance hormones naturally. Black pepper, rosemary, and marjoram can improve pain and increase blood flow.

sections.title: Infertility (female and male) — the Holistic Rx
body: If you have been having unprotected sex for at least one year and can't get pregnant, you or your partner may have primary infertility, or secondary infertility (inability to become pregnant or carry a pregnancy to term following the birth of one or more biological children). Causes span a broad range, from poor nutrition and environmental toxin exposure to hormonal issues or other medical conditions.

Female infertility supplements: vitex agnus-castus (chasteberry) (160–240 mg daily) helps stimulate the ovaries and balance estrogen and progesterone ratios. Vitamin B complex (50 mg daily) is important in estrogen metabolism. Vitamin E (400 IU daily). Evening primrose oil (1,500 mg once or twice daily from day 1 to day 14 of the menstrual cycle) supports fertility efforts. Natural progesterone cream (20 mg to the skin daily, started after ovulation and used under a doctor's guidance). Others: black cohosh; shatavari (600 mg of the root three times a day), an Ayurvedic remedy that helps promote reproductive health; tribulus (should contain at least 100 mg of the key active compound; can be taken three times daily on days 5 through 14 of the cycle); rhodiola (4.5 mg rosavins and 1.5 mg salidroside per dose, about two to three tablets per day) for anxiety and mental stress; ginger (ten to twenty drops in a warm cup of tea); and dong quai (tablet form, 1 g root equivalent, twice per day).

Male infertility supplements that improve sperm count, motility, and quality: L-arginine (2,000 mg twice daily on an empty stomach). Panax ginseng (300 mg), zinc (30 mg twice daily) along with copper (3–5 mg). Vitamin C (500 mg twice daily). Multivitamin. CoQ10 (200–300 mg per day). Vitamin C (500–1,000 mg per day). NAC (600 mg per day). L-carnitine (2,000–3,000 mg per day).

sections.title: Irregular periods and abnormal uterine bleeding — the Holistic Rx
body: A normally functioning ovary releases an egg every twenty-five to twenty-eight days; the uterus builds tissue in anticipation of implantation, and when that doesn't occur, it sheds the lining as menstruation. Regular, moderately pain-free periods each month are a sign that hormones are balanced. Irregular periods, missed periods, or very painful and intense PMS symptoms signal that one or more hormones are imbalanced. Diagnosis is made after a detailed history, exam, labs, and diagnostic tests. Causes of irregular periods include: high stress levels; a poor diet low in antioxidants and probiotic foods and high in sugar, hydrogenated fats, pesticides, or artificial additives/preservatives; extreme weight loss or gain; overexercising; thyroid disorders; PCOS; stopping the birth control pill; and food sensitivities or allergies. Balancing hormones is key to balancing irregular periods. Other signs of hormonal imbalance are infertility, weight gain or loss, depression and anxiety, sleep issues, low libido, fatigue, digestive issues, and hair loss/thinning. Specific problems associated with hormonal imbalance include estrogen dominance, PCOS, low estrogen, thyroid issues, diabetes, and adrenal fatigue.

Supplements for excessive menstrual bleeding: vitamin C (500–1,000 mg three times per day). Fish oil. Chasteberry extract. Bioflavonoids (1,000 mg per day). Others: chlorophyll (25 mg per day), iron (30 mg twice a day with meals), and chasteberry. For adolescents: first two weeks of the cycle, 1 tbsp flax and 1 tbsp pumpkin seeds; second two weeks, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 1 tbsp sunflower seeds, fish oil (2–4 g EPA/DHA per day), pycnogenol (50 mg daily), and chasteberry (5% vitexin, 20–40 mg daily).

Homeopathy for amenorrhea (temporary or permanent absence of periods) — can be taken every twelve hours for up to fourteen days: Aconite — periods stopped due to exposure to dry cold, or stopped suddenly from an emotional event. Calcarea — fatigue, legs feel heavy, swollen and painful breasts, anxiety. Dulcamara — periods stop after extraneous exercise that leaves the woman cold. Natrum muriaticum — constipation, irritability, headaches, thinning hair, recent emotional shock. Ignatia — periods stopped because of loss or grief. Sepia — weak, irritable, weepy, with abnormal vaginal discharge. Lycopodium — lower abdominal pain, headaches, sadness, dry vagina; slight emotional upsets disrupt the cycle. Ferrum — weak, tired, pale face, occasional hot flashes, wants to sit down all the time.

Homeopathy for abnormal bleeding: China — intermittent bleeding with abdominal cramps, faintness, pale face, giddiness, dark clots. Sabina — dark blood, bad labor-like back pain, difficulty controlling weight, with or without clots, emotional upsets, increased blood loss. Belladonna — regular periods with bright red blood, throbbing headache, hot and flushed face. Ipecac — profuse bright red bleeding with nausea. Calcarea — cramping abdominal pain, back pain, head congestion, weight problems, general paleness. Ferrum — dark, watery blood with a pale face, improved with walking. Crocus — sensation of movement inside the uterus, feels sick, worried, and weak, expels blackish clots. Kali carbonica — exhaustion, cold extremities, thin watery bleeding without clots, feeling of dying, worse with warmth. Borax — profuse bleeding with nausea and pelvic/abdominal cramps, especially the first day or two of the period, worse at night.
Acupressure: LI4 (pain and inflammation), SP10, SP6.

Aromatherapy: basil can improve delayed menstruation and scanty periods. Cypress can relieve stagnation associated with heavy bleeding or midcycle bleeding. Geranium has an overall balancing effect on female hormones.

sections.title: Menopause — the Holistic Rx
body: Menopause is a time in a woman's life when sex hormones start to decline due to the degeneration of the ovaries. Women can experience a wide variety of symptoms, from irregular periods, hot flashes, and night sweats to mood swings, irritability, depression, anxiety, vaginal dryness, increased abdominal fat, and thinning hair. With these hormonal changes, there is increasing loss of ovarian follicles and a decreased amount of estrogen produced; this begins about six to twelve months before menopause, in the late thirties and forties, and continues throughout the menopause process.

Supplements: black cohosh (80 mg one or two times daily) improves hormonal imbalances. Natural progesterone cream (about 20 mg applied to the skin of the wrists and forearms two to three times per day from days 14 to 25; if perimenopausal, 20 mg three to four weeks of the month; postmenopausal, 10 mg three weeks of the month) helps with fibroids and vaginal dryness. Vitex (160–240 mg) regulates hormones — don't take with oral contraceptive pills. American ginseng (600–1,200 mg daily). Red clover lowers risk of heart complications and loss of bone density, and improves hot flashes, weight issues, and sleep troubles. Others: hops (250 mg two to three times per day) for anxiety with mild hormone-balancing properties; the Chinese herb rehmannia (25–100 mg daily) reduces heart palpitations, hot flashes, and night sweats; evening primrose, licorice root, red raspberry leaves, wild yams, sarsaparilla, and chaste tree; DIM (diindolylmethane) (75–300 mg per day), omega-3, calcium D-glucarate, probiotics, plant phytoestrogens, resveratrol, black cohosh, melatonin, and SAMe. Chondroitin sulfate can be used for incontinence. Hot flashes: sage (three cups of tea per day), black cohosh (20 mg for twelve weeks), omega-3, flaxseed, vitamin E (400 mg per day). Heavy periods: yarrow (two droppers of tincture every thirty minutes until bleeding slows). Fatigue: ashwagandha (500 mg twice daily). Vaginal dryness: kudzu. Low sex drive: Peruvian maca root (500–1,000 mg per day), ArginMax for women (ginseng, ginkgo, multivitamin, minerals), L-arginine (improves circulation). Mood issues: St. John's wort. Adaptogenic herbs: maca root (1,000–2,000 mg daily) to improve stress, decrease cortisol, reduce hot flashes, and improve energy and libido; also ashwagandha, medicinal mushrooms, holy basil, and rhodiola.

Homeopathy: Amylium nitrosum — sudden onset of hot flashes followed by a sensation of coolness. Belladonna — throbbing symptoms in the head, sudden flushing, profuse sweating, restlessness, heat, palpitations, headaches on the right side. Bryonia — constipation with blackish or burned-looking stools, vagina dry and thin. Calcarea carbonica — overwhelmed, anxious, fatigued; night sweats/hot flashes, cold, leg cramps, heavy menses, weight gain during the transition. Kali carbonica — loss of appetite, hot flashes, palpitations, nervousness, backaches worse around 3:00 a.m. Graphites — hot flashes especially on the face, cutting abdominal pains, scanty periods, weight gain, nosebleeds. Lachesis — hot flashes, anxiety, headaches on waking, dizziness, flooding during periods, sleep issues, memory/concentration problems, palpitations worse lying on the left side; talkative, suspicious, jealous, angry; constricted around the abdomen, must avoid tight clothing at the neck. Natrum muriaticum — hot flashes and vaginal dryness, cries easily, depressed, craves salt and cold drinks, migraines and backaches, worse in the sun. Oophorinum — a specific remedy for hot flashes in women who have had their ovaries removed. Pulsatilla — hot flashes, hemorrhoids, varicosities; fair-haired, often cold, cries easily, prefers open air, worse in a warm room, craves chocolate and sweets. Sanguinaria canadensis — hot flashes that redden the cheeks and burn the ears, radiating to the palms and soles. Sepia — heavy menstrual periods, backache, sinking feeling in the pit of the stomach, anxiety, pain during intercourse; can help with prolapsed uterus, incontinence, and vaginal dryness; exhausted, irritable, tearful, craves sweets/chocolate or sour foods. Sulphur — hot flashes worse after exercise and at night, easily sweats, craves ice-cold drinks. Lachesis, Sulphur, and Sepia, already mentioned as constitutional remedies, also cover hot flushes in their pathogeneses. Bone and joint disorders associated with menopause: Kali carbonicum and Natrum sulphuricum. Osteoporosis: Silicea and Calcarea carbonica. Nervous disorders: Lachesis, Sepia, Sulphur, Thuja, Ignatia, Nux vomica, Aurum muriaticum. Vaginal dryness: Sepia and Lycopodium depending on symptoms.

Acupressure: LI4, GV24.5 (improve headaches and hot flashes). GV20 (headaches, clearing the mind). CV17 (sleep, hot flashes). P6, B60, GB20 (irritability, dizziness, stress, hot flashes). LI11 (hot flashes). H6 (night sweats, anxiety). LV3 (headaches, insomnia, mood changes). K3 (night sweats, mood disorders). SP6 (balance). CV6, CV17 (hot flashes, mood disorders).

Aromatherapy: rub three drops of the chosen oil on the tops of the feet and back of the neck one to three times per day. Hot flashes: clary sage, peppermint, geranium, cypress, lime; thyme oil can help balance hormones. Depression: bergamot, clary sage, cypress, geranium, grapefruit, jasmine, lavender, marjoram, neroli, niaouli, sweet orange, petitgrain, rose, or ylang-ylang. Mood swings and anxiety: bergamot, cedarwood, Roman chamomile, clary sage, frankincense, geranium, jasmine, lavender, mandarin, marjoram, sandalwood, or ylang-ylang. Stress: Roman chamomile.

sections.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) — the Holistic Rx
body: PCOS occurs when a woman's hormones are out of balance, leading to symptoms like weight gain and trouble losing weight, acne, irregular periods, thinning of scalp hair, extra hair on the face and body, depression, and fertility issues. Diagnosis occurs via history and examination, blood tests demonstrating insulin resistance and elevated testosterone, and imaging like ultrasound demonstrating ovarian cysts. Left untreated, PCOS increases the risk of developing diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and heart disease.

Additional integrative modalities: the underlying insulin resistance driving PCOS is managed with the diet, supplement, and lifestyle protocol described in the Insulin Resistance, Prediabetes, Metabolic Syndrome, and Diabetes entry (Endocrinology chapter) — glucose control, gut healing, and lowering toxin exposure are the core levers for rebalancing hormones in PCOS.

sections.title: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) — the Holistic Rx
body: PMS is common in about 75 percent of menstruating women. Symptoms include breast tenderness, mood instability and emotional changes, bloating, fatigue, cramping, and skin changes. Symptoms can start seven to ten days before the menstrual flow and end shortly after. Diagnosis is via history and physical.

Supplements: vitex (chasteberry) (240 mg daily) to balance hormone levels — don't take with oral contraceptive pills. Calcium carbonate (500 mg twice daily) for PMS prevention. Vitamin B6 (50–100 mg daily). Zinc (15–20 mg per day). Vitamin E (200–400 IU per day). Magnesium (250 mg twice daily). Natural progesterone cream (1/4 tsp or 10 mg applied twice daily to thin skin like the wrists, from the beginning of ovulation until the day before your period). Indole-3-carbinol (300 mg daily) aids estrogen metabolism. Dong quai (Angelica sinensis) (300–500 mg twice daily, on the last seven days of the cycle) helps with breast tenderness and cramps. Others: vitamin A (5,000 IU per day); B complex (with 50 mg of B6); evening primrose oil (500 mg twice daily); 5-HTP (50–100 mg twice daily) to boost serotonin and lower anxiety; green tea or L-tyrosine (500 mg two to three times daily); ginkgo biloba (80–160 mg twice daily); hypericum perforatum/St. John's wort (900–1,800 mg per day). Preteen/teen: calcium (800–2,000 mg daily), vitamin B1 (100 mg daily), vitamin B6 (20–40 mg daily), fish oil (EPA/DHA 2–4 g daily), magnesium (100–200 mg daily), vitamin D (1,000–4,000 IU per day), fennel extract liquid (thirty drops twice daily), ginkgo biloba leaf extract (50:1 ratio, 24% ginkgo heterosides, 6% terpene lactone, 80 mg daily), saffron (60 mg daily), valerian root (0.8% valerenic acid, 250 mg daily), and chasteberry (5% vitexin, 20–40 mg daily).

Homeopathy (take every twelve hours for up to three days, starting twenty-four hours before premenstrual symptoms): Calcarea carbonica — fatigue, cold sweats, anxiety, painful and swollen breasts; craves eggs and sweets, clammy chilly hands and feet. Matricaria chamomilla — unbearable, painful menses; irritable, angry, very sensitive to pain; better with motion, worse with warm applications. Cimicifuga — painful menses worsening as flow increases, cramping and shooting pains across the legs/thighs, headache, stiffness in neck and back. Causticum — irritable, pessimistic, frequent urination, symptoms of cystitis, colicky lower abdominal pain. Kali carbonicum — exhausted and tense, worse around 3:00 a.m., works best in overweight women. Lachesis — a major PMS remedy; symptoms worse in the morning with emotional issues (rage, jealousy, suspicion), painful breasts and abdomen improving once menses starts, irritated by anything touching the throat; headaches before periods aggravated by heat, sunshine, and alcohol, plus hot flushes; dosing schedule: Lachesis 9C on day 19 of the cycle, 15C on day 20, 30C on day 21. Lilium tigrinum — great irritability, crosses her legs for relief from a feeling that internal organs will prolapse, fresh air brings relief. Lycopodium — depressed, lacks self-confidence, irritable, digestive problems, craves sweets. Nux vomica — constipated, frequent urination, chilly, irritable, angry, craves coffee, alcohol, spicy or fatty foods; improves with warmth and rest. Pulsatilla — sudden bursts of tears, irritability, mood swings, painful breasts, irregular periods; improves with consolation and attention; craves sweets, especially chocolate; worse in warm rooms. Sepia — irritable, weepy, emotionally flat, feels uterus will fall out, breast tenderness, turned off by sex, craves salty and sweet foods; improves with exercise. Natrum muriaticum — fluid retention, swollen breasts, irritable and sad, lower back pain and migraines, craves salt, dislikes sun. Sulphur — for when the major PMS symptom is a craving for sweets. Specific symptoms: nervous symptoms — ignatia, Nux vomica, moschus, Murex purpurea, and cyclamen. Mastodynia — Lac caninum, phytolacca, Conium maculatum. Headaches — sanguinaria, Lac caninum. Venous disorders — Hamamelis, Vipera, Aesculus hippocastanum. ENT symptoms — Magnesia carbonica, Lac caninum. Skin issues/herpes — Rhus toxicodendron, borax, croton. Acne — Kali bromatum, Eugenia jambosa, Natrum muriaticum, sepia, sulphur, Calcarea carbonica. Water retention — Natrum muriaticum, Thuja occidentalis, Natrum sulphuricum. Hormone balance — Folliculinum (30C on the seventh or eighth day of the cycle).

Acupressure: LV3, SP4, SP6, GB34, ST29, B47, CV6 (improve pain), HP6. To relieve digestive complaints like diarrhea and constipation: CV6. For lower back pain: B25, B31, and B40. To ease tension and stress: LV3.

Aromatherapy: for abdominal cramps — black pepper and rosemary. To balance female hormones — geranium and rose oils. To reduce stress — geranium, rose oil, lavender, bergamot, or jasmine. To increase sexual desire — patchouli and ylang-ylang. Fluid retention — juniper compress.

sections.title: Vaginal yeast infection — the Holistic Rx
body: Yeast infection is a candidal infection of the vagina. Yeast infections occur in areas where yeast and fungus can thrive, in moist conditions like the mouth, throat, and genitals. When yeast overpopulates in the vagina, symptoms can include vaginal discharge — usually thick, white, clumpy (cottage-cheese-like), and odorless — along with irritated skin around the vaginal opening, painful intercourse, and pain when urinating or during menses. Diagnosis is confirmed via examination and culture collection.

Additional integrative modalities: use the full antifungal diet, supplement, and topical protocol described under Candidiasis (Gastroenterology chapter) — the same overgrowth-lowering approach applies to vaginal yeast infections.
